title: SHA changed on 7.1.2-2
need_summary: Whether the mismatched ImageMagick release archive SHA reflects a compromised or merely repackaged upstream release, with the answer anchored by the Homebrew pull request https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/pull/280403 switching downloads to GitHub releases.
security_topic: whether differing release archives indicate a compromised or messy release
question_text:
Hi @dlemstra 

The archives https://imagemagick.org/archive/releases/ImageMagick-7.1.2-21.tar.xz and https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/releases/download/7.1.2-21/ImageMagick-7.1.2-21.7z do not contain the same files. In fact, quite a lot of files differ including build-related files.

Can you provide reassurance that everything is okay?
answer_text: We had a bit of a messy release last time. I have created the following pull request to switch to GitHub releases: https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/pull/280403. I have tested this and the installation succeeded with those changes..

### Description

Homebrew asked to post this upstream, which I assume means here.

[git issue link](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-core/pull/278686#discussion_r3168137346)

While doing a brew install of imagemagick on an older mac, where it has to be build from source, the error comes up:

✘ Formula imagemagick-full (7.1.2-21)
Verifying    10.8MB/ 10.8MB
Error: Formula reports different checksum:  3da290f49318e52a7a663adf1837a468769d0f7db637d3567a26cfb2a52b4580
       SHA-256 checksum of downloaded file: 56450bf5d65b63abb09568abb2c40b493ab913418f92df135ed661471da0eb0d

Homebrew maintainers aren't going to change the SHA in the brew formula until they get verification that there is no compromise of the archive.

### Steps to Reproduce

brew install imagemagick --build-from-source



### Images

An image would just be a snapshot of the command line output.

title: High memory/cpu utilization when identifying heic image
need_summary: Whether the HEIC parsing issue causing huge memory/CPU usage was a security-relevant resource-exhaustion bug, and the answer rests on the linked libheif security-limit issue (#1777) and the patch described in comment c9.
security_topic: resource exhaustion when parsing HEIC/AVIF image metadata
question_text:
The identity command does not complete in a resonable amount of time and utilizes a lot of memory.

This failed instantly in 7.1.2-13
identify.exe: Invalid input: No or invalid primary item (2.124) `C038.heic' @ error/heic.c/IsHEIFSuccess/202.
answer_text:
This is caused because animated AVIF support was added recently (#8640). The image you are providing has `42949672` output samples and that takes ages to read. You can limit that with the following command:
```
magick -limit listlength 2 C038.heic info:
```

This will only allow 2 animation frames.

ISSUE #8690: Memory leak in SVGKeyValuePairs on allocation failure (CVE-2019-10649 follow-up)
Author: B67687
Date: 2026-04-23T12:17:38Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
## Summary

A memory leak in SVGKeyValuePairs() in coders/svg.c remains when AcquireMagickMemory() fails mid-loop during token allocation. This appears to be a follow-up to #1533 / CVE-2019-10649.

## Description

In SVGKeyValuePairs(), tokens are allocated in a loop:

`c
for (q=p; *q != '\0'; q++)
{
    // ...
    tokens[i]=(char *) AcquireMagickMemory((size_t) (q-p+2));
    if (tokens[i] == (char *) NULL)
      {
        (void) ThrowMagickException(...);
        break;  // <-- Previously allocated tokens are leaked
      }
    // ...
}
`

When AcquireMagickMemory() returns NULL, the code breaks out of the loop but **does not free tokens[0..i-1] or the tokens array itself**. This leaks memory proportional to the number of tokens already parsed.

## Impact

- DoS via memory exhaustion when processing malformed SVGs that trigger repeated allocation failures
- Long-running services (web servers, image processing pipelines) accumulate leaked memory

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run ImageMagick with AddressSanitizer/LeakSanitizer
2. Process an SVG that causes memory pressure during SVGKeyValuePairs()
3. Observe memory leak reports similar to #1533

## Additional Context

While investigating this, I also noticed two related defensive improvements that could be included:
- coders/tiff.c: buffer is freed but not nulled after RelinquishMagickMemory()
- coders/pdf.c: xref is freed in ThrowPDFException macro but not nulled

Both are preemptive hardening against potential double-free scenarios.

## Suggested Fix

On allocation failure, iterate backwards and DestroyString() all previously allocated tokens, then RelinquishMagickMemory(tokens) before returning NULL.

I have a patch ready and will submit a PR referencing this issue.

thread_text:
ISSUE #8584: NULL pointer dereference in WriteHEICImage when heif_nclx_color_profile_alloc fails
Author: aarushidwi
Date: 2026-02-27T20:44:07Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
## Description

`WriteHEICImage()` in `coders/heic.c` (line 1484) calls `heif_nclx_color_profile_alloc()` but does not check for a NULL return before dereferencing the pointer on lines 1485-1488. Under memory pressure or allocation failure, this causes a SIGSEGV (crash) at address `0x4`.

The bug is in the `heic:cicp` option handling path, conditionally compiled under `LIBHEIF_NUMERIC_VERSION >= HEIC_COMPUTE_NUMERIC_VERSION(1,17,0)`.

## Affected Version

- ImageMagick 7.1.2-15 (current `main`)
- Requires libheif >= 1.17.0

## Vulnerable Code

```c
// coders/heic.c:1484-1488
nclx_profile=heif_nclx_color_profile_alloc();
cicp.rho=(double) nclx_profile->color_primaries;         // crash if NULL
cicp.sigma=(double) nclx_profile->transfer_characteristics;
cicp.xi=(double) nclx_profile->matrix_coefficients;
cicp.psi=(double) nclx_profile->full_range_flag;
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build ImageMagick 7.1.2-15 with libheif >= 1.17.0
2. Create test image: `magick -size 100x100 xc:blue test.jpg`
3. Trigger under OOM conditions or with LD_PRELOAD stub that forces NULL return:
   ```
   LD_PRELOAD=./fake_heif.so magick test.jpg -define heic:cicp=1 output.heic
   ```
4. Observe: `SIGSEGV {si_signo=SIGSEGV, si_code=SEGV_MAPERR, si_addr=0x4}` → process crash (exit 134)

## Impact

- **CWE-476**: NULL Pointer Dereference
- **CVSS 6.5**: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- Denial of service — crashes the ImageMagick process, affecting any concurrent image processing

## Suggested Fix

Add a NULL check after allocation, consistent with ImageMagick conventions:

```c
nclx_profile=heif_nclx_color_profile_alloc();
if (nclx_profile == (struct heif_color_profile_nclx *) NULL)
  ThrowWriterException(ResourceLimitError,"MemoryAllocationFailed");
```

A PR with this fix is submitted: see linked PR.

title: SIGABRT (double-free) converting SVG with `gradientTransform` on `<linearGradient>`
need_summary: Whether the SVG `gradientTransform` double-free crash is a security-relevant memory-safety regression introduced by commit `9db96365e` (the GHSA-xpg8-7m6m-jf56 fix), and the answer rests on that commit plus the linked fix in #8583.
security_topic: double-free regression in SVG gradientTransform handling after a security fix
question_text: magick crashes with a double-free (SIGABRT, exit code 134) when converting any SVG containing a `gradientTransform` attribute on a `<linearGradient>` element. Removing the attribute makes conversion succeed. ImageMagick 6 is not affected.
answer_text:
### Root cause

Introduced in `9db96365e` (2026-02-15, tag `7.1.2-14`) — the security fix for GHSA-xpg8-7m6m-jf56.

That commit changed `value` in `SVGStartElement`'s attribute loop from a `const char *` alias (pointing directly into `attributes[i+1]`, never freed) to a heap-allocated `char *` via `SVGEscapeString()`, with `DestroyString(value)` added at the end of each iteration.

The `gradientTransform` and `transform` inner token-parsing loops have had `value=(char *) tokens[j+1]` since the SVG coder was first written (2009, `3ed852eea`). Before `9db96365e`, that was harmless — `value` wasn't owned memory. After, reassigning `value` inside the inner loop:
1. **Leaks** the original `SVGEscapeString()` allocation (pointer is clobbered)
2. **Double-frees** `tokens[j+1]` (freed once by the token cleanup loop, then again by `DestroyString(value)`)

Fix in #8583: use a separate `token_value` local in each inner loop.

ISSUE #8582: SIGABRT (double-free) converting SVG with `gradientTransform` on `<linearGradient>`
Author: ryan-williams
Date: 2026-02-27T02:29:27Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### Description

`magick` crashes with a double-free (SIGABRT, exit code 134) when converting any SVG containing a `gradientTransform` attribute on a `<linearGradient>` element. Removing the attribute makes conversion succeed. ImageMagick 6 is not affected.

### Error output

```
free(): double free detected in tcache 2
Aborted (core dumped)
```

### Minimal reproducer SVG

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="g" gradientTransform="matrix(1 0 0 1 0 0)" gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
      <stop offset="0" style="stop-color:red"/>
      <stop offset="1" style="stop-color:blue"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect fill="url(#g)" width="512" height="512"/>
</svg>
```

Removing `gradientTransform="matrix(1 0 0 1 0 0)"` (even though it's an identity matrix) makes the conversion succeed.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Save the SVG above as crash.svg, then:
magick crash.svg crash.png
# → exit code 134 (SIGABRT)
```

### CI repro

Full automated repro with GitHub Actions: https://github.com/ryan-williams/imagemagick-svg-crash

GHA run showing the crash: https://github.com/ryan-williams/imagemagick-svg-crash/actions/runs/22469220910

### Versions tested

| Version | Result |
|---|---|
| ImageMagick 7.1.2-16 (Beta), Ubuntu x86_64 (source build) | **crashes** (double-free) |
| ImageMagick 7.1.2-15, macOS arm64 (Homebrew) | **crashes** |
| ImageMagick 6.9.12-98, Ubuntu x86_64 (apt) | works fine |
| librsvg 2.58.0 (`rsvg-convert`) | works fine |

### Root cause

Introduced in `9db96365e` (2026-02-15, tag `7.1.2-14`) — the security fix for GHSA-xpg8-7m6m-jf56. That commit changed `value` in `SVGStartElement`'s attribute loop from a non-owned `const char *` alias to a heap-allocated `char *` via `SVGEscapeString()`, with `DestroyString(value)` added at the end of each iteration. The `gradientTransform` and `transform` inner token-parsing loops have reassigned `value` to `tokens[j+1]` since 2009 (`3ed852eea`); previously harmless, this now leaks the original allocation and double-frees the token.

Fix: #8583

### System info

Tested on macOS arm64 (Homebrew) and Ubuntu x86_64 (GHA). Both crash with IM7; IM6 works fine on both.

### Root cause

Introduced in `9db96365e` (2026-02-15, tag `7.1.2-14`) — the security fix for GHSA-xpg8-7m6m-jf56.

That commit changed `value` in `SVGStartElement`'s attribute loop from a `const char *` alias (pointing directly into `attributes[i+1]`, never freed) to a heap-allocated `char *` via `SVGEscapeString()`, with `DestroyString(value)` added at the end of each iteration.

The `gradientTransform` and `transform` inner token-parsing loops have had `value=(char *) tokens[j+1]` since the SVG coder was first written (2009, `3ed852eea`). Before `9db96365e`, that was harmless — `value` wasn't owned memory. After, reassigning `value` inside the inner loop:
1. **Leaks** the original `SVGEscapeString()` allocation (pointer is clobbered)
2. **Double-frees** `tokens[j+1]` (freed once by the token cleanup loop, then again by `DestroyString(value)`)

Fix in #8583: use a separate `token_value` local in each inner loop.

### Description

`magick` crashes with a double-free (SIGABRT, exit code 134) when converting any SVG containing a `gradientTransform` attribute on a `<linearGradient>` element. Removing the attribute makes conversion succeed. ImageMagick 6 is not affected.

### Error output

```
free(): double free detected in tcache 2
Aborted (core dumped)
```

### Minimal reproducer SVG

```xml
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 512 512">
  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="g" gradientTransform="matrix(1 0 0 1 0 0)" gradientUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
      <stop offset="0" style="stop-color:red"/>
      <stop offset="1" style="stop-color:blue"/>
    </linearGradient>
  </defs>
  <rect fill="url(#g)" width="512" height="512"/>
</svg>
```

Removing `gradientTransform="matrix(1 0 0 1 0 0)"` (even though it's an identity matrix) makes the conversion succeed.

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
# Save the SVG above as crash.svg, then:
magick crash.svg crash.png
# → exit code 134 (SIGABRT)
```

### CI repro

Full automated repro with GitHub Actions: https://github.com/ryan-williams/imagemagick-svg-crash

GHA run showing the crash: https://github.com/ryan-williams/imagemagick-svg-crash/actions/runs/22469220910

### Versions tested

| Version | Result |
|---|---|
| ImageMagick 7.1.2-16 (Beta), Ubuntu x86_64 (source build) | **crashes** (double-free) |
| ImageMagick 7.1.2-15, macOS arm64 (Homebrew) | **crashes** |
| ImageMagick 6.9.12-98, Ubuntu x86_64 (apt) | works fine |
| librsvg 2.58.0 (`rsvg-convert`) | works fine |

### Root cause

Introduced in `9db96365e` (2026-02-15, tag `7.1.2-14`) — the security fix for GHSA-xpg8-7m6m-jf56. That commit changed `value` in `SVGStartElement`'s attribute loop from a non-owned `const char *` alias to a heap-allocated `char *` via `SVGEscapeString()`, with `DestroyString(value)` added at the end of each iteration. The `gradientTransform` and `transform` inner token-parsing loops have reassigned `value` to `tokens[j+1]` since 2009 (`3ed852eea`); previously harmless, this now leaks the original allocation and double-frees the token.

Fix: #8583

### System info

Tested on macOS arm64 (Homebrew) and Ubuntu x86_64 (GHA). Both crash with IM7; IM6 works fine on both.

title: Regression at finding delegates on Windows
need_summary: Whether the Windows Ghostscript delegate quoting bug was fixed in ImageMagick 7.1.2-17, with the answer anchored by the updated `config/delegates.xml` output showing `"` quoting.
security_topic: Windows delegate command quoting regression
question_text: The real problem is that the generated `config/delegates.xml` file itself contains hardcoded single quotes (`'`) and the 32-bit executable name (`gswin32c`).
answer_text: This code has already been changed and we are now using a `DELEGATE_ESC` define that is `"` on Windows and `'` on other platforms.
thread_text:
ISSUE #8574: Regression at finding delegates on Windows
Author: larskanis
Date: 2026-02-22T12:41:34Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

ImageMagick 7.1.2-12 Q16-HDRI aarch64

### Operating system

Windows

### Operating system, version and so on

Windows 11 ARM64 but the same happens on X64

### Description

Commit https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/commit/ac73bd3fcf7aaaf6beab8f69e91a8080f35134de changed `delegates.xml` to use single quotes instead of previous double quotes. But single quotes are not recognized by the Windows `cmd.exe`, when executing the command line, but double quotes only.

Error is like so:
```
$ magick  spec\fixtures\sample.pdf test.png
magick: FailedToExecuteCommand `'quot;gswin32c'quot; -sstdout=%stderr -dQUIET -dSAFER -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -dNOPROMPT -dMaxBitmap=500000000 -dAlignToPixels=0 -dGridFitTT=2 'quot;-sDEVICE=png16malpha'quot; -dTextAlphaBits=4 -dGraphicsAlphaBits=4 'quot;-r72x72'quot; -dPrinted=false  'quot;-sOutputFile=C:/Users/Lars/AppData/Local/Temp/magick-jIjHF2tbIcpqVptgpKqV1rR030EakO1R%d'quot; 'quot;-fC:/Users/Lars/AppData/Local/Temp/magick-caalUBOJwSnpFG_vppM15GU1W7Jd4wGA'quot; 'quot;-fC:/Users/Lars/AppData/Local/Temp/magick-qhdS9-fSFMrPdbjc9DE5O7hpa-V0XDo3'quot;' (127) @ error/ghostscript-private.h/ExecuteGhostscriptCommand/75.
magick: PDFDelegateFailed `Das System kann die angegebene Datei nicht finden.
' @ error/pdf.c/ReadPDFImage/713.
```

Workaround is something like this:
```
$ sed "s/\'/\"/g" -i  C:/msys64/clangarm64/etc/ImageMagick-7/delegates.xml
$ magick  spec\fixtures\sample.pdf test.png
[... no error anymore]
```

This issue is also raised on MSYS2 here: https://github.com/msys2/MINGW-packages/issues/27003


### Steps to Reproduce

Make sure ghostscript is installed. For instance from the MSYS2 repository:
```
pacman -S mingw-w64-clang-aarch64-ghostscript
```


### Images

[sample.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25468566/sample.pdf)

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @dlemstra 2026-02-22T15:06:58Z:
This code has already been changed and we are now using a `DELEGATE_ESC` define that is `"` on Windows and `'` on other platforms.

comments.body:
### ImageMagick version

ImageMagick 7.1.2-12 Q16-HDRI aarch64

### Operating system

Windows

### Operating system, version and so on

Windows 11 ARM64 but the same happens on X64

### Description

Commit https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/commit/ac73bd3fcf7aaaf6beab8f69e91a8080f35134de changed `delegates.xml` to use single quotes instead of previous double quotes. But single quotes are not recognized by the Windows `cmd.exe`, when executing the command line, but double quotes only.

Error is like so:
```
$ magick  spec\fixtures\sample.pdf test.png
magick: FailedToExecuteCommand `'quot;gswin32c'quot; -sstdout=%stderr -dQUIET -dSAFER -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -dNOPROMPT -dMaxBitmap=500000000 -dAlignToPixels=0 -dGridFitTT=2 'quot;-sDEVICE=png16malpha'quot; -dTextAlphaBits=4 -dGraphicsAlphaBits=4 'quot;-r72x72'quot; -dPrinted=false  'quot;-sOutputFile=C:/Users/Lars/AppData/Local/Temp/magick-jIjHF2tbIcpqVptgpKqV1rR030EakO1R%d'quot; 'quot;-fC:/Users/Lars/AppData/Local/Temp/magick-caalUBOJwSnpFG_vppM15GU1W7Jd4wGA'quot; 'quot;-fC:/Users/Lars/AppData/Local/Temp/magick-qhdS9-fSFMrPdbjc9DE5O7hpa-V0XDo3'quot;' (127) @ error/ghostscript-private.h/ExecuteGhostscriptCommand/75.
magick: PDFDelegateFailed `Das System kann die angegebene Datei nicht finden.
' @ error/pdf.c/ReadPDFImage/713.
```

Workaround is something like this:
```
$ sed "s/\'/\"/g" -i  C:/msys64/clangarm64/etc/ImageMagick-7/delegates.xml
$ magick  spec\fixtures\sample.pdf test.png
[... no error anymore]
```

This issue is also raised on MSYS2 here: https://github.com/msys2/MINGW-packages/issues/27003


### Steps to Reproduce

Make sure ghostscript is installed. For instance from the MSYS2 repository:
```
pacman -S mingw-w64-clang-aarch64-ghostscript
```


### Images

[sample.pdf](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25468566/sample.pdf)

Hi @dlemstra

Thank you for your work on this!
Although this issue is closed, the problem still persists on MSYS2/MinGW environments.
I have investigated the root cause and would like to share my findings to help fix it permanently.

title: Potential NULL Pointer Dereference in MagickCore
need_summary: Whether the reported null pointer dereference issues in ImageMagick were confirmed and fixed in 7.1.2.15, based on the maintainer’s reproduction and patch announcement.
security_topic: null pointer dereference validity and fix status
question_text:
Hello ImageMagick maintainers,

While reviewing the source code of ImageMagick, we identified several potential NULL pointer dereference issues. To avoid wasting your time, we carefully analyzed the relevant execution paths and manually reviewed the affected code sections, and we believe these cases may be triggerable under certain conditions. We would greatly appreciate your feedback on whether they are considered valid.
answer_text: Thank you for reporting the issue. We have successfully reproduced it and are actively working on a patch to resolve the issue. You can expect this patch to be merged into the [main GIT branch](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick), later today. As part of our commitment to quality, this fix will also be included in the upcoming [beta releases of ImageMagick](https://imagemagick.org/archive/beta/) by tomorrow. Your patience and feedback are greatly appreciated.

comments.author: ylwango613
comments.body:
Maybe there are two potential NPD, the alpha-as-PNG path around line 12356 and the main JDAT-writing path around line 12732.
In coders/png.c in WriteOneJNGImage(), two ImageToBlob() results were originally used without an immediate NULL check and could cause a null-pointer dereference if ImageToBlob() fails but the code still passes blob to WriteBlob()/crc32().
In contrast, other coders typically add a guard right after ImageToBlob(), for example coders/cals.c around line 570, coders/pdf.c around line 1104, coders/ps3.c around line 311, and coders/magick.c around line 13279.

ISSUE #8538: Integer Overflow in FITS Image Dimension Parsing
Author: ylwango613
Date: 2026-01-22T05:17:31Z
Labels:

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

7.1.2-13

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system, version and so on

22.04.5 64bit

### Description

During FITS parsing, NAXIS1 and NAXIS2 (image width and height) are first multiplied as int values to compute the total number of pixels; when the values are large, this arithmetic overflows and yields an incorrect pixel count. This can cause the program to crash or abort parsing (denial of service), or lead to excessive memory allocation and potential out-of-bounds access.

### Steps to Reproduce

### PoC
use the following fits:
[[fits.gsfc.nasa.gov/samples/WFPC2u5780205r_c0fx.fits](https://fits.gsfc.nasa.gov/samples/WFPC2u5780205r_c0fx.fits)](https://fits.gsfc.nasa.gov/samples/WFPC2u5780205r_c0fx.fits)

Use the follow py file to transfer it to 65536*65537
```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
from typing import Tuple, Dict

FITS_BLOCK = 2880
CARD = 80

def _read_cards(buf: bytes, max_cards: int = 4096) -> Tuple[list[bytes], int]:
    """
    Read cards from buf[0:] in 80-byte increments until finding the END card (keyword == 'END').
    Returns (cards, header_len_bytes), where header_len_bytes is the padded header length (2880-aligned).
    """
    cards = []
    end_index = None

    # Need to at least cover up to END; typically primary header won't be too long, setting an upper limit here
    for i in range(0, min(len(buf), max_cards * CARD), CARD):
        card = buf[i:i + CARD]
        if len(card) < CARD:
            break
        cards.append(card)
        keyword = card[0:8].decode("ascii", errors="replace").rstrip()
        if keyword == "END":
            end_index = i + CARD
            break

    if end_index is None:
        raise ValueError("Cannot find END card in the first part of the file (primary header seems corrupted).")

    # Total header length needs to be padded to 2880 boundary (ImageMagick code will read the padding)
    header_len = ((end_index + FITS_BLOCK - 1) // FITS_BLOCK) * FITS_BLOCK
    return cards, header_len

def _parse_key_value(card: bytes) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    """
    Parse the keyword and value string from a card (as lenient as possible).
    """
    kw = card[0:8].decode("ascii", errors="replace").strip()
    rest = card[8:].decode("ascii", errors="replace")
    return kw, rest

def _get_int_value_from_card_rest(rest: str) -> int | None:
    """
    Extract an integer from the card[8:] string (handles '= <num>' format).
    """
    s = rest
    if len(s) == 0:
        return None
    if s[0] != "=":
        return None
    # Skip "= ", then strip
    s = s[1:]
    if s.startswith(" "):
        s = s[1:]
    s = s.strip()
    # Value may have a comment "/ ..."
    if "/" in s:
        s = s.split("/", 1)[0].strip()
    # FITS integers are typically right-aligned and may have a sign
    try:
        return int(s, 10)
    except ValueError:
        return None

def _format_int_card(keyword: str, value: int, comment: str = "") -> bytes:
    """
    Generate a standard FITS 80-byte card: KEYWORD= <value> / comment
    Note: keyword must be <=8 bytes and ASCII.
    """
    kw = (keyword[:8]).ljust(8)
    rhs = f"= {value:20d}"  # Common FITS format: numeric field width 20
    if comment:
        rhs += f" / {comment}"
    rhs = rhs[:72].ljust(72)
    card = (kw + rhs).encode("ascii", errors="strict")
    if len(card) != CARD:
        raise AssertionError("card length is not 80 bytes")
    return card

def _extract_primary_header_fields(cards: list[bytes]) -> Dict[str, int]:
    fields: Dict[str, int] = {}
    for c in cards:
        kw, rest = _parse_key_value(c)
        kw_low = kw.lower()
        if kw_low in ("bitpix", "naxis", "naxis1", "naxis2", "naxis3", "simple"):
            v = _get_int_value_from_card_rest(rest)
            if v is not None:
                fields[kw_low] = v
    return fields

def patch_naxis(in_path: str, out_path: str, new_naxis1: int, new_naxis2: int) -> None:
    data = open(in_path, "rb").read()

    cards, header_len = _read_cards(data)
    fields = _extract_primary_header_fields(cards)

    if "bitpix" not in fields:
        raise ValueError("BITPIX not found in primary header; cannot compute data size safely.")
    if "naxis" not in fields:
        raise ValueError("NAXIS not found in primary header.")
    bitpix = fields["bitpix"]
    naxis = fields["naxis"]

    if naxis < 2:
        # You're now changing NAXIS1/2; if naxis<2, the FITS primary HDU isn't a 2D image
        # ImageMagick code also requires rows/columns > 0 to proceed
        # Here we directly set NAXIS to 2 (conservative approach)
        naxis = 2

    if bitpix == 0 or (abs(bitpix) % 8) != 0:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported BITPIX={bitpix} for this patcher (expect 8/16/32/64/-32/-64).")
    bytes_per_pixel = abs(bitpix) // 8

    if new_naxis1 <= 0 or new_naxis2 <= 0:
        raise ValueError("new NAXIS1/NAXIS2 must be positive.")

    # --- Modify header cards (don't change card count/total bytes, only modify corresponding card content)
    def replace_or_append(keyword: str, value: int):
        nonlocal cards
        key_upper = keyword.upper()
        replaced = False
        for idx, c in enumerate(cards):
            kw = c[0:8].decode("ascii", errors="replace").strip().upper()
            if kw == key_upper:
                cards[idx] = _format_int_card(key_upper, value)
                replaced = True
                break
        if not replaced:
            # Inserting a new card before END: this would change header length and subsequent offsets.
            # To "never break the structure", we don't insert.
            # In actual FITS, NAXIS1/2 should exist; if not, the original file is very atypical.
            raise ValueError(f"{key_upper} card not found; refusing to insert cards (would shift the file).")

    # If needed, first set NAXIS to 2 (prerequisite: NAXIS card originally exists)
    if "naxis" in fields:
        replace_or_append("NAXIS", naxis)
    else:
        raise ValueError("NAXIS card not found; cannot safely patch without shifting.")

    replace_or_append("NAXIS1", new_naxis1)
    replace_or_append("NAXIS2", new_naxis2)

    # --- Reassemble header and maintain its length as the original header_len (2880-aligned)
    new_header = b"".join(cards)
    if len(new_header) > header_len:
        # Theoretically won't happen (we didn't insert cards)
        raise ValueError("Patched header unexpectedly exceeds original padded header length.")
    new_header = new_header.ljust(header_len, b" ")

    # --- Handle primary data unit
    old_data = data[header_len:]
    new_data_bytes = new_naxis1 * new_naxis2 * bytes_per_pixel

    # Conservative: only ensure the primary data area is long enough; don't handle extensions (if the original file has extensions, changing dimensions may cause semantic inconsistency)
    if len(old_data) < new_data_bytes:
        new_data = old_data + (b"\x00" * (new_data_bytes - len(old_data)))
    else:
        new_data = old_data[:new_data_bytes]

    # Extra: pad data to 2880 per FITS convention (not mandatory, but more standard)
    pad = (-len(new_data)) % FITS_BLOCK
    if pad:
        new_data += b"\x00" * pad

    with open(out_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(new_header)
        f.write(new_data)

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 5:
        print(f"Usage: {sys.argv[0]} <in.fits> <out.fits> <new_naxis1> <new_naxis2>")
        sys.exit(2)

    in_path, out_path = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
    n1, n2 = int(sys.argv[3]), int(sys.argv[4])
    patch_naxis(in_path, out_path, n1, n2)
    print("OK:", out_path)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```
yuelinwang@XXF-GPU-03:/data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/ImageMagick/test++$ python3 112.py 112.fits 112+.fits 65536 65537
OK: 114.fits
```

Use magick to read file
```
./utilities/magick /data/ylwang/LargeScan/targets/ImageMagick/test++/112+.fits null
coders/fits.c:420:56: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 65536 * 65537 cannot be represented in type 'int'
coders/fits.c:436:54: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 65536 * 65537 cannot be represented in type 'int'
```

title: Insecure File Access Due to External Control of Environment Variables in Magick++
need_summary: Whether the path traversal via SRCDIR/MAGICK_FONT can be mitigated by ImageMagick’s documented security policy that denies file reads outside an allowed directory.
security_topic: path traversal via environment-variable-controlled file paths
question_text: The `getenv` function is used to read environment variables `SRCDIR` and `MAGICK_FONT`, which are external inputs controllable by the user. The `SRCDIR` variable is used to construct a file path that is passed directly to the `Image` constructor to read a file. Due to the lack of validation and sanitization for these inputs, an attacker could manipulate the environment variables to include path traversal sequences (e.g., `../../`) to access arbitrary files. This leads to potential unauthorized access to sensitive files through the application's output.
answer_text:
ImageMagick uses this pattern in its demos and test utilities, but these executables are **not** included in a standard installation. When the code is used independently, developers can harden it by sanitizing any user‑controlled paths before passing them to ImageMagick.

As an additional layer of protection, a user may restrict ImageMagick’s filesystem access by denying all reads except those from explicitly allowed directories. A [security policy](https://imagemagick.org/script/security-policy.php) such as the following can enforce this:

```xml
<policymap>
  <!-- Deny all file reads by default -->
  <policy domain="path" rights="none" pattern="*" />

  <!-- Allow reads ONLY from /opt/ImageMagick/ -->
  <policy domain="path" rights="read" pattern="/opt/ImageMagick/*" />
</policymap>
```

How this policy works

- Global deny rule — Blocks all filesystem reads (pattern="*").
- Allow rule — Re‑enables read access only for files located under /opt/ImageMagick/.

All other paths, including system directories such as /etc/, /home/, /var/, and any relative path traversal attempts like ../../,  are denied.

title: Regression: JPEG with density_unit=0 interpreted as 1 DPI instead of aspect ratio
need_summary: Whether JPEG JFIF density_unit=0 should be treated as undefined resolution rather than 1 DPI, with the maintainer confirming a patch was pushed for the regression introduced after issue #8375.
security_topic: JPEG JFIF density_unit=0 resolution interpretation regression
question_text: After the fix for issue #8375 (commits 5e3b82d8a, bb9038036, d98902116 on Oct 5, 2025), ImageMagick now incorrectly interprets JPEG files with `density_unit=0` (aspect ratio mode) and `X_density=1, Y_density=1` as having a resolution of "1x1 DPI" instead of recognizing these as aspect ratio values with undefined resolution.
answer_text: Thanks for reporting this. I just pushed a patch that fixes this issue and it will be resolved in the next release.
thread_text:
ISSUE #8460: Regression: JPEG with density_unit=0 interpreted as 1 DPI instead of aspect ratio
Author: akohring
Date: 2025-11-24T18:13:35Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

7.1.2.8-r0

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system, version and so on

Alpine v3.22

### Description

## Summary

After the fix for issue #8375 (commits 5e3b82d8a, bb9038036, d98902116 on Oct 5, 2025), ImageMagick now incorrectly interprets JPEG files with `density_unit=0` (aspect ratio mode) and `X_density=1, Y_density=1` as having a resolution of "1x1 DPI" instead of recognizing these as aspect ratio values with undefined resolution.

## Version Information

- **Affected Version**: ImageMagick 7.1.2-5 and later (after Oct 5, 2025 commits)
- **Previous Working Version**: 7.1.2-3 and earlier
- **Regression introduced by**: Commits 5e3b82d8a, bb9038036, d98902116 (fix for issue #8375)

## Expected Behavior

According to the JFIF specification:
- When `density_unit = 0`, the X_density and Y_density fields represent **pixel aspect ratio**, NOT actual resolution in DPI
- A JPEG with `density_unit=0, X_density=1, Y_density=1` means "1:1 aspect ratio (square pixels) with no resolution information"
- ImageMagick should either:
  - Ignore these values and use a sensible default (e.g., 72 DPI), OR
  - Report that resolution is truly undefined/unknown

**Version 7.1.2-3 behavior** (worked correctly):
```bash
$ magick identify -units PixelsPerInch -format "%w,%h,%x,%y" test.jpg
"4096,2669,72,72"
```

## Actual Behavior

**Current version behavior** (regression):
```bash
$ magick identify -units PixelsPerInch -format "%w,%h,%x,%y" test.jpg
"4096,2669,1,1"

$ magick identify -verbose test.jpg
...
Resolution: 1x1
Units: Undefined
...
```

ImageMagick now reads the aspect ratio values (1:1) as if they were resolution values, resulting in "1 DPI" which is incorrect.


## Technical Details

### JFIF Header Hex Dump

The test JPEG file has the following JFIF header values:
```bash
$ xxd -s 13 -l 1 -p test.jpg
00                    # density_unit = 0 (Undefined/Aspect ratio)

$ xxd -s 14 -l 2 -p test.jpg
0001                  # X_density = 1

$ xxd -s 16 -l 2 -p test.jpg
0001                  # Y_density = 1
```

### Root Cause

The current code in `coders/jpeg.c` (after d98902116):

```c
if (jpeg_info->saw_JFIF_marker != 0)
  {
    if (jpeg_info->X_density != 0)
      image->resolution.x=(double) jpeg_info->X_density;
    if (jpeg_info->Y_density != 0)
      image->resolution.y=(double) jpeg_info->Y_density;
    if (jpeg_info->density_unit != 0)
      units=(size_t) jpeg_info->density_unit;
  }
```

**Problem**: This code reads X_density and Y_density values even when `density_unit=0` (aspect ratio mode), where they should NOT be interpreted as resolution values.

### The Regression Timeline

1. **Pre-Oct 2025** (7.1.2-3 and earlier): Code skipped reading density when either value was 1:
   ```c
   if ((jpeg_info->saw_JFIF_marker != 0) && (jpeg_info->X_density != 1) &&
       (jpeg_info->Y_density != 1))
   ```
   - Side effect: Ignored aspect ratio values, used default 72 DPI ✓

2. **Oct 5, 2025** (Issue #8375 fix): Removed the `!= 1` check to fix reading of actual DPI values of 1
   - Side effect: Now reads aspect ratio values as if they were DPI values ✗

## Suggested Fix

The code should check `density_unit` BEFORE reading density values:

```c
if (jpeg_info->saw_JFIF_marker != 0)
  {
    if (jpeg_info->density_unit != 0)  // Only read if units are actually defined
      {
        if (jpeg_info->X_density != 0)
          image->resolution.x=(double) jpeg_info->X_density;
        if (jpeg_info->Y_density != 0)
          image->resolution.y=(double) jpeg_info->Y_density;
        units=(size_t) jpeg_info->density_unit;
      }
    // When density_unit=0, leave resolution unset (aspect ratio only)
  }
```

This would properly distinguish between:
- Files with actual DPI info (`density_unit=1` for DPI or `density_unit=2` for DPC)
- Files with only aspect ratio info (`density_unit=0`) - should be ignored for resolution purposes

## Impact

This regression affects:
- Any JPEG files with `density_unit=0` and density values of 1 (very common for images without embedded resolution data)
- Tools and workflows that rely on ImageMagick to extract or convert resolution information
- Users upgrading from 7.1.2-3 to newer versions will see resolution change from 72 DPI to 1 DPI for these files

## Related Issues

- #8375 - The fix that introduced this regression
- #7120 - Related to density 0x0 problems
- #228 - density_unit being set to 0 unexpectedly

## JFIF Specification Reference

From the JFIF specification:
> **units**: 1 byte
> - 0 = no units, X and Y specify the pixel aspect ratio
> - 1 = X and Y are dots per inch
> - 2 = X and Y are dots per cm

When `units=0`, the density values are explicitly defined as aspect ratio, not resolution.

## Test Case

Sample JPEG file characteristics:
- Dimensions: 4096x2669 pixels
- JFIF density_unit: 0 (Undefined/Aspect ratio)
- JFIF X_density: 1
- JFIF Y_density: 1
- Expected interpretation: 1:1 pixel aspect ratio, resolution undefined/default
- Actual interpretation: 1x1 DPI (incorrect)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Create or obtain a JPEG file with the following JFIF header:
   - `density_unit = 0` (no units/aspect ratio mode)
   - `X_density = 1`
   - `Y_density = 1`

2. Run the identify command:
```bash
magick identify -units PixelsPerInch -format "%w,%h,%x,%y" test.jpg
```

3. Observe that X and Y resolution are reported as "1,1" instead of a sensible default

### Images

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9f28edc-4d1e-425b-872e-48b6db575638)

[c1] @dlemstra 2025-11-24T21:17:38Z:
Thanks for reporting this. I just pushed a patch that fixes this issue and it will be resolved in the next release.
---

title: Apple ProRAW format failing with JPEG-XL (lossy) "raw" files due to routing to LibRaw
need_summary: Whether Apple ProRAW DNG files with JPEG-XL data are unsupported because ImageMagick routes them through LibRaw, and the answer rests on LibRaw’s README.DNGSDK.txt plus the maintainer’s explanation that support requires a custom LibRaw build.

question_text:
Do you think that should be done by default by ImageMagick, or at least implemented behind a compilation flag?

If not, I'd appreciate any help with building a version of ImageMagick that supports those files :)
answer_text: So this means that you would need to build your own version of libraw that has support for this? Not sure why you think we should handle this. And you should also be careful with using the Adobe DNG SDK because it does not appear to have a license file.
thread_text:
ISSUE #8440: Apple ProRAW format failing with JPEG-XL (lossy) "raw" files due to routing to LibRaw
Author: galaxyeden
Date: 2025-11-11T12:20:24Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

ImageMagick 7.1.2-8 Q16-HDRI aarch64 23412

### Operating system

MacOS

### Operating system, version and so on

macOS Tahoe 26.1

### Description

We first observed this with Immich running in a Debian 13 container which uses ImageMagick 7.1.2, but I've reproduced it independently on my Mac so that we can do any other tests needed.

ImageMagick sends all `DNG` files to [LibRaw](https://www.libraw.org/) to be parsed. The result is that an Apple ProRAW file with JPEG-XL image data errors with `Unsupported file format or not RAW file` coming from LibRaw.

I'm opening this as an ImageMagick issue because I believe that it is likely possible to support these without upstream support from LibRaw since the data in the DNG container is JPEG-XL, which ImageMagick can otherwise handle. There may be issues with metadata support and correct exposure/color grading – I'm no expert on this, but it feels like a bug that a supported data format isn't at least partially supported because the container format is routed to LibRaw.

Credit to @ember-ana for running the Immich server we identified this on and for their assistance with debug info from their Immich server.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `magick identify IMG_2025.DNG` with the attached image

Output:
```
identify: Unsupported file format or not RAW file `IMG_2025.DNG' @ error/dng.c/ReadDNGImage/508.
```

comments.author: galaxyeden
comments.body:
### ImageMagick version

ImageMagick 7.1.2-8 Q16-HDRI aarch64 23412

### Operating system

MacOS

### Operating system, version and so on

macOS Tahoe 26.1

### Description

We first observed this with Immich running in a Debian 13 container which uses ImageMagick 7.1.2, but I've reproduced it independently on my Mac so that we can do any other tests needed.

ImageMagick sends all `DNG` files to [LibRaw](https://www.libraw.org/) to be parsed. The result is that an Apple ProRAW file with JPEG-XL image data errors with `Unsupported file format or not RAW file` coming from LibRaw.

I'm opening this as an ImageMagick issue because I believe that it is likely possible to support these without upstream support from LibRaw since the data in the DNG container is JPEG-XL, which ImageMagick can otherwise handle. There may be issues with metadata support and correct exposure/color grading – I'm no expert on this, but it feels like a bug that a supported data format isn't at least partially supported because the container format is routed to LibRaw.

Credit to @ember-ana for running the Immich server we identified this on and for their assistance with debug info from their Immich server.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `magick identify IMG_2025.DNG` with the attached image

Output:
```
identify: Unsupported file format or not RAW file `IMG_2025.DNG' @ error/dng.c/ReadDNGImage/508.
```

### Images

An image that will create this issue is:

[IMG_2025.DNG.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23477805/IMG_2025.DNG.zip)

title: identify on a JPG with JFIF units set to cm or inches does not get shown as such, if the density is 1
need_summary: Whether ImageMagick’s identify/magick handling of JFIF density units set to 1 was a bug and how it was fixed in the referenced block in coders/jpeg.c, with the anchor being the linked source line in the main branch.
security_topic: incorrect JPEG JFIF units handling in identify/magick
question_text:
If you don't trust `exiftool` you can also just `hexdump -C` the resulting jpg.  The jpg output is definitely `cm` Units and `identify` is reporting it incorrectly.

But the other part of the bug is that the output from `magick` is also invalid because `-units undefined` should have set `undefined`, and not `cm`.

If you want it to work correctly, you can run `magick bug.png -strip fix.png` first, and then the jpg steps work properly.
answer_text: Thank you for reporting the issue. We have successfully reproduced it and are actively working on a patch to resolve the issue. You can expect this patch to be merged into the [main GIT branch](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick), later today. As part of our commitment to quality, this fix will also be included in the upcoming [beta releases of ImageMagick](https://imagemagick.org/archive/beta/) by tomorrow. Your patience and feedback are greatly appreciated.
thread_text: ISSUE #8375: identify on a JPG with JFIF units set to cm or inches does not get shown as such, if the density is 1 Author: johnkw Date: 2025-10-02T16:51:45Z Labels: State: closed [c0] ### ImageMagick version 7.1.1-47 ### Operating system Linux ### Operating system, version and so on Fedora ### Description The JFIF header is really CM, at least as far as my reading of the spec goes there's no other way to interpret that 0x02 byte. But identify gets it wrong. If you -strip the PNG and make a temp PNG, this behavior goes away. I'm not sure what flag or data magick is getting from the original PNG, so I'm including a sample PNG with the bug, but there's not anything particularly unusual about this PNG. I cropped it down to 1 pixel and that was enough. ``` $ magick bug.png -units undefined -density 1 bug.jpg $ identify -verbose bug.jpg |grep Units Units: Undefined $ exiftool -list bug.jpg |grep 'Resolution Unit' Resolution Unit : cm ``` https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d5e38f3-9a97-4e9c-af32-bb5233621b6b --- COMMENTS --- [c1] @fmw42 2025-10-02T17:06:53Z: Your question is not very clear to me. What is wrong with your output? EXIFTOOL may default to cm when the units are undefined. Please post an image that works the way you think it should and one that does not. --- [c2] @johnkw 2025-10-02T18:48:10Z: If you don't trust `exiftool` you can also just `hexdump -C` the resulting jpg. The jpg output is definitely `cm` Units and `identify` is reporting it incorrectly. But the other part of the bug is that the output from `magick` is also invalid because `-units undefined` should have set `undefined`, and not `cm`. If you want it to work correctly, you can run `magick bug.png -strip fix.png` first, and then the jpg steps work properly. --- [c3] @fmw42 2025-10-03T04:10:57Z: When you -strip, IM will set default units that are not undefined. When you use units=undefined, IM cannot determine the correct units for you, nor the density. Exiftool may not recognize undefined or if it does, it overwrites it with the perhaps cm as PNG default units are cm. It is not that I do not trust Exiftool. It is correct. It does what it does. IM references the image as in IM memory. Exiftool references what is in the file on disk. However, I will defer to the IM developers for more details and accuracy on what is happening. --- [c4] @dlemstra 2025-10-03T15:33:31Z: We seem to not read the density when a jpeg file has both the x and y value set to 1. And I have no clue why we have that check. This has been like that since the start of our git history. --- [c5] @johnkw 2025-10-03T15:34:25Z: The file on disk is wrong. You can look at `hexdump -C` and compare against the JFIF spec to confirm this bug in `identify`. As for why `magick` writes the incorrect JPG, seemingly in defiance of `-units` I don't know. --- [c6] @dlemstra 2025-10-03T15:51:27Z: As I said in my previous message we completely ignore the density data when the x and y value are at 1. So that also means we don't read the units. I don't know why we do that but we have been doing that since at least 2009. Maybe this one odd exception where we should ignore the data but I cannot find anything about that online. So I don't know if we should change this. --- [c7] @johnkw 2025-10-03T16:00:44Z: Sorry my https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/issues/8375#issuecomment-3366207344 was directed more to the fmw42 comment, and just happened to post right after your comment posted. Where is that code oddity located? --- [c8] @dlemstra 2025-10-03T17:01:55Z: It's this block: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/blob/badaa5c3582a340484941903fa26419b5807d0df/coders/jpeg.c#L1185-L1190 --- [c9] @johnkw 2025-10-03T17:33:08Z: I found the origin of this bug, ha: https://sourceforge.net/p/graphicsmagick/code/ci/ecc5b5ec92b2d9d87140dc45297b2795113ceea4/ This bug is over 25 years old. Impressive. --- [c10] @fmw42 2025-10-03T17:41:32Z: Perhaps, but that link is to GraphicsMagick, not Imagemagick. GraphicsMagick split off from Imagemagick a long time ago. --- [c11] @dlemstra 2025-10-03T17:42:11Z: That is probably not even the origin because in this patch the check was changed from a double to an integer but still for `1` and this code from GraphicsMagick that is a fork of this project. So it is probably even older and that is why I am not sure if we should change it. --- [c12] @johnkw 2025-10-03T18:17:50Z: The cause of the bug wasn't the switch from float to int, it was the removal of `(jpeg_info.density_unit != 0) || `. When that was there, the 1 comparisons didn't cause an issue, and whenever a unit was set, the unit was loaded correctly. He also accidentally changed the || to &&, although that was just compounding one bug with another. --- [c13] @johnkw 2025-10-03T18:18:56Z: (And yes, it's from before the project fork, over 25 years ago. GraphicsMagick also inherited this bug.) --- [c14] @urban-warrior 2025-10-05T15:42:44Z: Thank you for reporting the issue. We have successfully reproduced it and are actively working on a patch to resolve the issue. You can expect this patch to be merged into the [main GIT branch](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick), later today. As part of our commitment to quality, this fix will also be included in the upcoming [beta releases of ImageMagick](https://imagemagick.org/archive/beta/) by tomorrow. Your patience and feedback are greatly appreciated. --- [c15] @johnkw 2025-10-05T15:58:27Z: Thanks but are you sure that `units=1;` is correct? It looks like in the case of JFIF density undefined, then magick is still going to incorrectly change over to DPI. --- [c16] @urban-warrior 2025-10-05T16:13:24Z: If density is undefined we default to 72DPI which is what is used by virtually every other format. What do you think the default should be if resolution of units is not defined? --- [c17] @johnkw 2025-10-05T16:16:54Z: Well the spec says undefined is that there is no defined association with inches or centimeters at all. After the above commit, isn't `magick` going to take a units=undefined JPEG, and re-write it as a DPI jpeg? Surely we'd want by default the units=undefined JPEGs to stay units=undefined unless otherwise requested to change via the `-units` command line option. --- [c18] @johnkw 2025-10-05T16:44:09Z: Thanks, although that also seems odd to me. Why were these removed? ``` image->resolution.x=(double) jpeg_info->X_density; image->resolution.y=(double) jpeg_info->Y_density; units=(size_t) jpeg_info->density_unit; ``` Those 3 lines seemed correct. Now it seems like `image->resolution.x` is always going to end up as zero whenever `density_unit` is zero. (The aspect ratio calculation just seems to risk additional errors also. Simply always setting the resolution x/y to equal the density x/y seems safer surely?) --- [c19] @johnkw 2025-10-06T15:14:43Z: Thanks. So I got the github head and this fixes the bug in `identify` so that's good. The new output appears to be correct to me as far as the JFIF standard goes: ``` $ diff -U0 <(identify -verbose bug.jpg) <(~/bin/identify -verbose bug.jpg) --- /dev/fd/63 2025-10-06 13:50:27.833443285 +0000 +++ /dev/fd/62 2025-10-06 13:50:27.834443314 +0000 @@ -8 +8,3 @@ - Units: Undefined + Resolution: 1x1 + Print size: 1x1 + Units: PixelsPerCentimeter @@ -94 +96 @@ - Pixels per second: 9934P + Pixels per second: 7548P @@ -97 +99 @@ - Version: ImageMagick 7.1.1-47 Q16-HDRI x86_64 22763 https://imagemagick.org + Version: ImageMagick 7.1.2-5 Q16-HDRI x86_64 7d94ecf41:20251005 https://imagemagick.org ``` However specifying `-units undefined` on the `magick` command line still doesn't remove the units flag from the output. I moved that to a new bug #8389 so this can just be for the `identify` issue. ---

title: MAGICK_TIME_LIMIT ignored when SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is in use
need_summary: Whether MAGICK_TIME_LIMIT is bypassed when SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is set, and the maintainer says a patch is being merged into the main GIT branch.
security_topic: timeout enforcement disabled when SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is set
question_text:
When updating rubygem-mini_magick (a Ruby wrapper of ImageMagick) package for Fedora, I was struggling with following test failure during the build of package:

~~~

ISSUE #8301: MAGICK_TIME_LIMIT ignored when SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is in use
Author: voxik
Date: 2025-08-14T12:28:43Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

7.1.1.47

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system, version and so on

Fedora Rawhide

### Description

When updating rubygem-mini_magick (a Ruby wrapper of ImageMagick) package for Fedora, I was struggling with following test failure during the build of package:

~~~
  1) MiniMagick::Shell#run terminate long running commands if timeout is set
     Failure/Error:
       expect { subject.run(%W[convert #{image_path} -resize 10000x10000 -blur 0x20 null:], timeout: 1) }
         .to raise_error(MiniMagick::TimeoutError)

       expected MiniMagick::TimeoutError but nothing was raised
     # ./spec/lib/mini_magick/shell_spec.rb:45:in 'block (3 levels) in <top (required)>'
~~~

The issues is that the timeout set by `MAGICK_TIME_LIMIT` is not respected. For a while, I couldn't reproduce this manually and it failed just during the package build. As it turns out, during the build, there is set `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and when it is set, the `MAGICK_TIME_LIMIT` does not work.

### Steps to Reproduce

~~~
$ SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1755043200 MAGICK_TIME_LIMIT=1 time convert spec/fixtures/default.jpg -resize 10000x10000 -blur 0x20 null:
WARNING: The convert command is deprecated in IMv7, use "magick" instead of "convert" or "magick convert"

155.66user 0.89system 0:24.39elapsed 641%CPU (0avgtext+0avgdata 2563200maxresident)k
0inputs+0outputs (0major+644882minor)pagefaults 0swaps
~~~

~~~
$ MAGICK_TIME_LIMIT=1 time convert spec/fixtures/default.jpg -resize 10000x10000 -blur 0x20 null:
WARNING: The convert command is deprecated in IMv7, use "magick" instead of "convert" or "magick convert"

convert: time limit exceeded `spec/fixtures/default.jpg' @ error/cache.c/GetImagePixelCache/1699.
Command exited with non-zero status 1
6.15user 0.56system 0:01.24elapsed 539%CPU (0avgtext+0avgdata 1713820maxresident)k
0inputs+0outputs (0major+432566minor)pagefaults 0swaps
~~~

### Images

https://github.com/minimagick/minimagick/blob/master/spec/fixtures/default.jpg

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @voxik 2025-08-14T12:33:19Z:
BTW, the workaround for me as easy as precede the test suite with `env -u SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`. It just took me by surprise
---
[c2] @snibgo 2025-08-14T12:50:11Z:
`convert` is deprecated. Use `magick` instead.

The problem also occurs under Windows 11, IM v7.1.1-20.
```
set MAGICK_TIME_LIMIT=1

magick xc: -resize 10000x10000 -blur 0x20 null:
```
The process correctly terminates with:
```
magick: time limit exceeded `' @ fatal/cache.c/GetImagePixelCache/1707.
```
However, if we first do this...
```
set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1755043200
```
... then the time limit is not correctly checked.

---
[c3] @urban-warrior 2025-08-15T23:51:01Z:
Thank you for reporting the issue. We have successfully reproduced it and are actively working on a patch to resolve the issue. You can expect this patch to be merged into the [main GIT branch](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick), later today. As part of our commitment to quality, this fix will also be included in the upcoming [beta releases of ImageMagick](https://imagemagick.org/archive/beta/) by tomorrow. Your patience and feedback are greatly appreciated.

thread_text:
ISSUE #8265: `compare -metric AE` reports difference for the same image on arm64 (and other platforms with fused multiply-add)
Author: zhaofengli
Date: 2025-07-20T20:50:00Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
> [!NOTE]
> Fixed in 2d055c2, with a fixup in 95eb90d.

### ImageMagick version

7.1.2-0

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system, version and so on

NixOS 25.11 unstable (Linux 6.12.31), macOS 26.0 beta (25A5306g)

### Description

On arm64, ImageMagick reports difference when comparing the same image with `-metric AE`. The image must have an alpha channel:

```console
# To generate the image:
$ magick logo: -alpha set -channel Alpha -evaluate set 50% -resize 60 small.png

# Repro:
$ uname -sm
Linux aarch64
$ magick compare -verbose -metric AE small.png small.png null:
small.png PNG 60x45 60x45+0+0 8-bit PaletteAlpha sRGB 116c 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
small.png PNG 60x45 60x45+0+0 8-bit PaletteAlpha sRGB 116c 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
Image: small.png
  Channel distortion: AE
    red: 1
    green: 0.99037
    blue: 0.99037
    alpha: 0
    all: 1
small.png=> PNG 60x45 8-bit sRGB 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
```

On x86-64, IM returns 0 as expected. The commit that first revealed the issue is f6b8ed1a5d6748d272d8839398d7ed6475bcae5f.

Turning off floating-point contraction with `-ffp-contract=off` fixes the issue. Should we add it for arm64 builds? Alternatively, we can treat very small differences as zero.

## Longer Explanation

The underlying issue is not specific to ImageMagick and appears to be caused by fused multiply-add, which is enabled by default in both GCC and Clang. Compile the following code:

```c
// cc -O2 -g -o repro ./repro.c
// cc -O2 -g -ffp-contract=off -o repro.nofma ./repro.c

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>

void __attribute__ ((noinline)) make_magic(double *a) {
  *a = 0.1;
}

int main() {
  double a, b, c, d;
  make_magic(&a);
  make_magic(&b);
  make_magic(&c);
  make_magic(&d);

  double diff = a * b - c * d;
  printf("%.20f, %s\n", diff, diff == 0.0 ? "zero :)" : "not zero :/");
}
```

Obviously `diff` should be zero. On Linux x86-64 (GCC defaults to not emitting FMA code):
```console
$ uname -sm
Linux x86_64
$ gcc --version
gcc (GCC) 14.3.0
[...]
$ gcc -O2 -g -o repro ./repro.c && ./repro
0.00000000000000000000, zero :)
```

However, on Linux aarch64:
```console
$ uname -sm
Linux aarch64
$ gcc --version
gcc (GCC) 14.3.0
[...]
$ gcc -O2 -g -o repro ./repro.c && ./repro
-0.00000000000000000083, not zero :/
$ gcc -O2 -ffp-contract=off -g -o repro.nofma ./repro.c && ./repro.nofma
0.00000000000000000000, zero :)
```

On macOS aarch64 using Clang from Xcode:
```console
$ clang --version
Apple clang version 17.0.0 (clang-1700.3.10.950)
Target: arm64-apple-darwin25.0.0
Thread model: posix
InstalledDir: /Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/bin
$ clang -O2 -g -o repro ./repro.c && ./repro
-0.00000000000000000083, not zero :/
$ clang -O2 -ffp-contract=off -g -o repro.nofma ./repro.c && ./repro.nofma
0.00000000000000000000, zero :)
```

### With Fused Multiply-Add

By default, Clang 17 [emits](https://godbolt.org/z/K697sxEac) the following code (`d0` is non-zero):

```
ldp d1, d0, [sp]
...
fnmul d0, d0, d1
ldr d1, [sp, #16]
fmadd d0, d2, d1, d0
```

In other words, it performs the following steps, with a rounding happening at each step:
1. `c_d_negated = -(c * d)`
2. `diff = (a * b) + c_d_negated`

Or `round((a * b) + round(-(c * d)))`

### Without Fused Multiply-Add

With `-ffp-contract=off` it [emits](https://godbolt.org/z/Pbax7M17M) (`d0` is zero as expected):

```
ldp d2, d1, [sp, #8]
ldur d0, [x29, #-8]
ldr d3, [sp]
fmul d0, d0, d1
fmul d1, d2, d3
fsub d0, d0, d1
```

Effectively it performs:

1. `a_b = a * b`
2. `c_d = c * d`
3. `diff = a_b - c_d`

Or `round(round(a * b) - round(c * d))`

Note the difference in rounding between the two.

<details>
<summary>Misunderstanding</summary>

<s>Naively it appears that the negation from `fnmul`/`fnmsub` causes the problem.</s> Edit: This was a misunderstanding. I have corrected the analysis above.
</details>

### Steps to Reproduce

```console
# To generate the image:
$ magick logo: -alpha set -channel Alpha -evaluate set 50% -resize 60 small.png

# Repro:
$ uname -sm
Linux aarch64
$ magick --version
Version: ImageMagick 7.1.2-0 Q16-HDRI aarch64 9bde76f1d:20250712 https://imagemagick.org
Copyright: (C) 1999 ImageMagick Studio LLC
License: https://imagemagick.org/script/license.php
Features: Cipher DPC HDRI OpenMP(4.5)
Delegates (built-in): bzlib cairo djvu fftw fontconfig freetype heic jng jp2 jpeg jxl lcms lqr lzma openexr pangocairo png raqm raw rsvg tiff webp x xml zlib zstd
Compiler: gcc (14.3)
$ magick compare -verbose -metric AE small.png small.png null:
small.png PNG 60x45 60x45+0+0 8-bit PaletteAlpha sRGB 116c 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
small.png PNG 60x45 60x45+0+0 8-bit PaletteAlpha sRGB 116c 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
Image: small.png
  Channel distortion: AE
    red: 1
    green: 0.99037
    blue: 0.99037
    alpha: 0
    all: 1
small.png=> PNG 60x45 8-bit sRGB 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
```

### Images

```
magick logo: -alpha set -channel Alpha -evaluate set 50% -resize 60 small.png
```

--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @fmw42 2025-07-20T21:06:04Z:
Alpha channel in magick compare is currently being worked on. The last release needed to get out and this had not been finished.

I get the same as you with the current 7.1.2.1 beta on Mac OSX Venture on M1 Mac.

```
magick compare -metric AE small.png small.png null:
2700 (1)

```


---
[c2] @zhaofengli 2025-07-20T21:17:34Z:
This worked before, and arm64 is the only platform where it started to fail recently. For context, what led me to the issue were the `test_png_rgba8` and `test_png_gray8a` tests in [img2pdf](https://gitlab.mister-muffin.de/josch/img2pdf).

The `repro.c` I gave above is intended to reproduce the same logic in `compare.c`:

https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/blob/6c7c8d5866b9c0ce6cc76a741e05b9482716101e/MagickCore/compare.c#L399

Anyways, the issue does not appear when building with `-ffp-contract=off`.
---
[c3] @fmw42 2025-07-20T21:22:58Z:
It may have worked before. But we have implemented new features in magick compare and this was not finished and the latest release had to get out. I suspect it will be fixed in an upcoming release soon.
---
[c4] @snibgo 2025-07-21T09:55:46Z:
On Windows 11, Intel processor, with Cygwin gcc toolset, I copied the source repro.c and built it in my usual way:
```
  gcc -o "$1" "$1".c -IMagickCore -I. -I../OpenCL-SDK/external/OpenCL-Headers -DMAGICKCORE_OPENCL_SUPPORT -std=c11 -Wconversion -Wanalyzer-use-after-free -Wpedantic -Wextra -Wall -Wunused-variable -Warray-bounds -Wunused-parameter -Warray-parameter -Wdeprecated -Ofast -m64 -march=native -mtune=native -Wall -Wunused-parameter -Warray-parameter -Wdeprecated -Wc++-compat -Wdeclaration-after-statement `pkg-config --cflags --libs MagickCore` -ldl -lpthread -L/usr/lib64/nvidia -L/usr/lib/nvidia
```
The program output is:
```
-0.00000000000000000083, not zero :/
```
Adding `-ffp-contract=off` fixes the problem.

Does this mean there is a bug in the CPU fused multiply-add? Or in the compiler? Of course, floating-point doesn't have infinite precision, so floating-point operations are often slightly incorrect mathematically, and code should be written to allow for this.

---
[c5] @zhaofengli 2025-07-21T16:29:18Z:
> Does this mean there is a bug in the CPU fused multiply-add? Or in the compiler?

I looked a bit more and it's a difference in rounding that causes the issue (see the updated post), so it's neither a bug in the CPU nor one in the compiler. [IEEE-754](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~vinals/tspot_files/phys4041/2020/IEEE%20Standard%20754-2019.pdf) has:

> A language standard should also define, and require implementations to provide, attributes that allow and
disallow value-changing optimizations, separately or collectively, for a block. These optimizations might
include, but are not limited to:
> ― ...
> ― Synthesis of a fusedMultiplyAdd operation from a multiplication and an addition.

So languages have leeway to apply this optimization.

> Of course, floating-point doesn't have infinite precision, so floating-point operations are often slightly incorrect mathematically, and code should be written to allow for this.

I agree. In the long run, I think disabling fused multiply-add gives up optimization opportunities where it's helpful, and similar floating-point issues can crop up elsewhere.

---

> On Windows 11, Intel processor, with Cygwin gcc toolset, I copied the source repro.c and built it in my usual way:
> `-march=native`

Oh I totally missed this. I re-tested and the same issue does occur on X86-64 when the target platform supports FMA:

```console
$ gcc -O2 -march=x86-64-v3 -g -o repro ./repro.c && ./repro
-0.00000000000000000083, not zero :/
```

It [emits](https://godbolt.org/z/hnzcafY96) code similar to the pathological case on arm64.
---
[c6] @urban-warrior 2025-07-22T00:11:23Z:
Disable OpenMP, add `--disable-openmp` to your configure CLI and rebuild and reinstall ImageMagick.  Does that resolve the issue?
---
[c7] @fmw42 2025-07-22T00:27:39Z:
I recompiled without OpenMP in 7.1.2.0 and still get 

```
magick compare -metric AE small.png small.png null:
2700 (1)

```

comments.author: zhaofengli
comments.body:
> [!NOTE]
> Fixed in 2d055c2, with a fixup in 95eb90d.

### ImageMagick version

7.1.2-0

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system, version and so on

NixOS 25.11 unstable (Linux 6.12.31), macOS 26.0 beta (25A5306g)

### Description

On arm64, ImageMagick reports difference when comparing the same image with `-metric AE`. The image must have an alpha channel:

```console
# To generate the image:
$ magick logo: -alpha set -channel Alpha -evaluate set 50% -resize 60 small.png

# Repro:
$ uname -sm
Linux aarch64
$ magick compare -verbose -metric AE small.png small.png null:
small.png PNG 60x45 60x45+0+0 8-bit PaletteAlpha sRGB 116c 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
small.png PNG 60x45 60x45+0+0 8-bit PaletteAlpha sRGB 116c 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
Image: small.png
  Channel distortion: AE
    red: 1
    green: 0.99037
    blue: 0.99037
    alpha: 0
    all: 1
small.png=> PNG 60x45 8-bit sRGB 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
```

On x86-64, IM returns 0 as expected. The commit that first revealed the issue is f6b8ed1a5d6748d272d8839398d7ed6475bcae5f.

Turning off floating-point contraction with `-ffp-contract=off` fixes the issue. Should we add it for arm64 builds? Alternatively, we can treat very small differences as zero.

## Longer Explanation

The underlying issue is not specific to ImageMagick and appears to be caused by fused multiply-add, which is enabled by default in both GCC and Clang. Compile the following code:

```c
// cc -O2 -g -o repro ./repro.c
// cc -O2 -g -ffp-contract=off -o repro.nofma ./repro.c

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>

void __attribute__ ((noinline)) make_magic(double *a) {
  *a = 0.1;
}

int main() {
  double a, b, c, d;
  make_magic(&a);
  make_magic(&b);
  make_magic(&c);
  make_magic(&d);

  double diff = a * b - c * d;
  printf("%.20f, %s\n", diff, diff == 0.0 ? "zero :)" : "not zero :/");
}
```

Obviously `diff` should be zero. On Linux x86-64 (GCC defaults to not emitting FMA code):
```console
$ uname -sm
Linux x86_64
$ gcc --version
gcc (GCC) 14.3.0
[...]
$ gcc -O2 -g -o repro ./repro.c && ./repro
0.00000000000000000000, zero :)
```

However, on Linux aarch64:
```console
$ uname -sm
Linux aarch64
$ gcc --version
gcc (GCC) 14.3.0
[...]
$ gcc -O2 -g -o repro ./repro.c && ./repro
-0.00000000000000000083, not zero :/
$ gcc -O2 -ffp-contract=off -g -o repro.nofma ./repro.c && ./repro.nofma
0.00000000000000000000, zero :)
```

On macOS aarch64 using Clang from Xcode:
```console
$ clang --version
Apple clang version 17.0.0 (clang-1700.3.10.950)
Target: arm64-apple-darwin25.0.0
Thread model: posix
InstalledDir: /Applications/Xcode-beta.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/bin
$ clang -O2 -g -o repro ./repro.c && ./repro
-0.00000000000000000083, not zero :/
$ clang -O2 -ffp-contract=off -g -o repro.nofma ./repro.c && ./repro.nofma
0.00000000000000000000, zero :)
```

### With Fused Multiply-Add

By default, Clang 17 [emits](https://godbolt.org/z/K697sxEac) the following code (`d0` is non-zero):

```
ldp d1, d0, [sp]
...
fnmul d0, d0, d1
ldr d1, [sp, #16]
fmadd d0, d2, d1, d0
```

In other words, it performs the following steps, with a rounding happening at each step:
1. `c_d_negated = -(c * d)`
2. `diff = (a * b) + c_d_negated`

Or `round((a * b) + round(-(c * d)))`

### Without Fused Multiply-Add

With `-ffp-contract=off` it [emits](https://godbolt.org/z/Pbax7M17M) (`d0` is zero as expected):

```
ldp d2, d1, [sp, #8]
ldur d0, [x29, #-8]
ldr d3, [sp]
fmul d0, d0, d1
fmul d1, d2, d3
fsub d0, d0, d1
```

Effectively it performs:

1. `a_b = a * b`
2. `c_d = c * d`
3. `diff = a_b - c_d`

Or `round(round(a * b) - round(c * d))`

Note the difference in rounding between the two.

<details>
<summary>Misunderstanding</summary>

<s>Naively it appears that the negation from `fnmul`/`fnmsub` causes the problem.</s> Edit: This was a misunderstanding. I have corrected the analysis above.
</details>

### Steps to Reproduce

```console
# To generate the image:
$ magick logo: -alpha set -channel Alpha -evaluate set 50% -resize 60 small.png

# Repro:
$ uname -sm
Linux aarch64
$ magick --version
Version: ImageMagick 7.1.2-0 Q16-HDRI aarch64 9bde76f1d:20250712 https://imagemagick.org
Copyright: (C) 1999 ImageMagick Studio LLC
License: https://imagemagick.org/script/license.php
Features: Cipher DPC HDRI OpenMP(4.5)
Delegates (built-in): bzlib cairo djvu fftw fontconfig freetype heic jng jp2 jpeg jxl lcms lqr lzma openexr pangocairo png raqm raw rsvg tiff webp x xml zlib zstd
Compiler: gcc (14.3)
$ magick compare -verbose -metric AE small.png small.png null:
small.png PNG 60x45 60x45+0+0 8-bit PaletteAlpha sRGB 116c 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
small.png PNG 60x45 60x45+0+0 8-bit PaletteAlpha sRGB 116c 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
Image: small.png
  Channel distortion: AE
    red: 1
    green: 0.99037
    blue: 0.99037
    alpha: 0
    all: 1
small.png=> PNG 60x45 8-bit sRGB 1130B 0.000u 0:00.000
```

### Images

```
magick logo: -alpha set -channel Alpha -evaluate set 50% -resize 60 small.png
```

comments.author: zhaofengli
comments.body:
> Does this mean there is a bug in the CPU fused multiply-add? Or in the compiler?

I looked a bit more and it's a difference in rounding that causes the issue (see the updated post), so it's neither a bug in the CPU nor one in the compiler. [IEEE-754](https://www-users.cse.umn.edu/~vinals/tspot_files/phys4041/2020/IEEE%20Standard%20754-2019.pdf) has:

> A language standard should also define, and require implementations to provide, attributes that allow and
disallow value-changing optimizations, separately or collectively, for a block. These optimizations might
include, but are not limited to:
> ― ...
> ― Synthesis of a fusedMultiplyAdd operation from a multiplication and an addition.

So languages have leeway to apply this optimization.

> Of course, floating-point doesn't have infinite precision, so floating-point operations are often slightly incorrect mathematically, and code should be written to allow for this.

I agree. In the long run, I think disabling fused multiply-add gives up optimization opportunities where it's helpful, and similar floating-point issues can crop up elsewhere.

---

> On Windows 11, Intel processor, with Cygwin gcc toolset, I copied the source repro.c and built it in my usual way:
> `-march=native`

This modification effectively reverted the changes made in the [de884e5 commit](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/commit/de884e5cf43d3580f33a4a5214c983474ba4a25c) to the type-dejavu.xml file, allowing ImageMagick-7.1.1-47 to successfully download SVG files.

title: time limit in policy.xml is not honoured
need_summary: Whether ImageMagick’s time resource limit is still enforced after the policy.xml bug, and the maintainer’s answer points to the upcoming main-branch patch plus explains the current stop behavior in cache.c/GetImagePixelCache and the image-based ttl setting.
security_topic: time limit enforcement delay in ImageMagick resource policy
question_text:
i have set custom policy [policy.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20532587/policy.txt) with time limit and configured the $MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH to point to it.

output of `magick -list policy` shows my custom policy is loaded. [magick_list_policy.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20532607/magick_list_policy.txt)

but `magick -list resource` shows time as unlimited
```
Resource limits:
  Width: 100000P
  Height: 100000P
  Area: 25MP
  List length: 100B
  Memory: 1GiB
  Map: 2GiB
  Disk: unlimited
  File: 786432
  Thread: 3
  Throttle: 0
  Time: unlimited
```
while doing some resize operation also, time limit is not honoured.|
this dosent happen with 7.1.0-60, where if the time limit exceeds, "time limit exceeded" exception is thrown
answer_text:
There is a delay because we don't use a signal to abort the process. When the pixels of the image are being access we check if a time limit has been hit and when that happens we stop executing of the next commands.

We don't communicate release dates because we don't know when it will happen. We are preparing for a new release but we cannot give you the exact date that it will happen.

ISSUE #8149: Signed integer TIFF files
Author: snibgo
Date: 2025-05-12T12:41:06Z
Labels: bug
State: closed

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

7.1.1-38 and older versions, eg 7.1.1-20

### Operating system

Windows

### Operating system, version and so on

Windows 11

### Description

There is a bug in reading or writing signed integer TIFF files.

Writing seems to be okay, but reading the file seems to incorrectly process the file as *unsigned*.

I don't know if the bug is in ImageMagick coders/tiff.c or in libtiff.


### Steps to Reproduce

To demonstrate the problem, we make two versions (signed and unsigned TIFF) of a 60% gray image, then convert each to a PNG file. The PNG of the unsigned tiff is correctly 60% gray. The PNG of the signed tiff is incorrectly 10% gray.

Make two tiff files:
```
magick -size 100x100 xc:gray(60%%) -define quantum:format=signed s.tiff
magick -size 100x100 xc:gray(60%%) -define quantum:format=unsigned u.tiff
```
Check the format with exiftool:
```
exiftool s.tiff |grep -i format
Sample Format                   : Signed    <== Correct

exiftool u.tiff |grep -i format
Sample Format                   : Unsigned    <== Correct
```
When viewing s.tiff and u.tiff in Microsoft Photo, the images look the same, as they should.

Make PNG versions:
```
magick s.tiff s2.png
magick u.tiff u2.png

magick s2.png -verbose info:

  Channel statistics:
    Pixels: 10000
    Gray:
      min: 6553  (0.0999924)    <== WRONG
      max: 6553 (0.0999924)     <== WRONG
      mean: 6553 (0.0999924)    <== WRONG


magick u2.png -verbose info:

  Channel statistics:
    Pixels: 10000
    Gray:
      min: 9  (0.6)      <== Correct
      max: 9 (0.6)       <== Correct
      mean: 9 (0.6)      <== Correct
```


### Images

s2.png is wrong:
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b97f05d8-cb1e-4786-81c5-c94cd07c2b60)

u2.png is correct:

See also: [ImageMagick/discussions/8147](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/discussions/8147)
---

It looks like we only support importing `SignedQuantumFormat` pixels in one specific case. Support for reading more cases will need to be added by someone.
---

Turns out that specific case was causing your issue. I just pushed a patch to remove that case to fix your issue. This will be resolved in the next release.

title: Magick++ Compositing small thumbnail images resutls in corruption
need_summary: Whether the compositing corruption was caused by missing background initialization, and the answer rests on the maintainer’s source-backed instruction to add `img.read("xc:transparent")` after `image.size()`.
security_topic: image compositing corruption due to missing background initialization
question_text: When using Magick++ to compile multiple images the result is corrupted.  These are tiny images (400 x 400px).
answer_text:
You need to properly define the image background.  Add

```
img.read("xc:transparent");
```
Right after 'image.size()'.

comments.body:
### ImageMagick version

ImageMagick 7.1.1-47 Q16-HDRI x86_64 22763

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system, version and so on

Arch (Linux 6.12.25-1-lts)

### Description

When using Magick++ to compile multiple images the result is corrupted.  These are tiny images (400 x 400px).

Creating a vector of several Image objects (all the same size) and then iterating through it to place one image on top of another will result in an image being corrupted.

In the example a cut out png image is further masked and composited before being placed on a drawn background. 

 



### Steps to Reproduce

`

    Magick::Image &composite = imPaths.front();

    for (Magick::Image &im : imPaths) {

        if (im != imPaths.front()) {

            composite.composite(im, MagickCore::CenterGravity, MagickCore::OverCompositeOp);

        }

    }

`

A workaround of sorts is to add a time delay (implying a mutex/thread issue of some sort).  Another workaround is to enlarge the images before processing.

`

    Magick::Image &composite = imPaths.front();

    for (Magick::Image &im : imPaths) {

        if (im != imPaths.front()) {

            composite.composite(im, MagickCore::CenterGravity, MagickCore::OverCompositeOp);
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(10));

        }

    }

`
will result in the image being rendered correctly.  In my application the original image is masked to be the same shape as the ellipse, it is then overlaid on a drawing of the ellipse.

ISSUE #8124: regression: json output contains nan as a bare word
Author: josch
Date: 2025-04-28T23:17:15Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

7.1.1-47-99-g7e3f3ae3d

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system, version and so on

Debian unstable

### Description

Hi,

apologies that this is amongst the issues that are still in the process of getting fixed. If so, please feel free to close this issue immediately. In the process of finding out whether ImageMagick git HEAD fixes the regressions I found in #8120 I ran into a problem that looks like #1112 which was supposedly fixed in 2018. Since this also didn't happen before, I tracked down the commit that started writing `nan` as a numeric value into the json output: 417dde7d4782295378d72831950805fbe4ecd217

If the value is indeed not a number, it would be nice if `NaN` was printed instead of `nan`. The former is understood by, for example, the python json parser while the latter is not:

    $ python3 -c 'import json;v=json.loads("NaN");print(v,type(v))'
    nan <class 'float'>

### Steps to Reproduce

Using the image attached below, the diff between the json output from before commit 417dde7d4782295378d72831950805fbe4ecd217 and after is:

```diff
--- before.json	2025-04-28 23:01:28.611480927 +0000
+++ after.json	2025-04-28 23:15:55.905102570 +0000
@@ -35,7 +35,7 @@
         "standardDeviation": 106.006,
         "kurtosis": -1.00199,
         "skewness": 0.91509,
-        "entropy": 0
```

title: libheif need overwrite max_memory_block_size for more large image
need_summary: Whether libheif’s security memory limit for large AVIF files should be overridden in ImageMagick, with the answer anchored on the libheif API in issue #1275 and ImageMagick’s planned use of `system:max-memory-request`.
security_topic: security limit override for large AVIF/HEIF image decoding
question_text:
Opening a large avif file report "Memory allocation error: Security limit exceeded: Allocating 668774415 bytes exceeds the security limit of 536870912 bytes (6.1000) "

### Describe the solution you'd like

Please add overwriting max_memory_block_size in heic.c/HEICSecurityLimits .
answer_text: Thanks for mentioning this. We had some patches in place for the security limits in heic but your comment just reminded me of a change that I had to make for this specific setting. In the next release the limit will be set to the `system:max-memory-request` that we have inside ImageMagick.
