Okay, so this is a limit set in heif/libheif/heif_limits.h:
```
static const int MAX_MEMORY_BLOCK_SIZE = 512 * 1024 * 1024; // 512 MB
```
To override this limit, libheif source code would need to be modified, either to increase this constant, or to make it a variable that could then be modified by ImageMagick code.

https://github.com/strukturag/libheif/issues/1275 says:
```
There is now an API to control the security limits. To switch them off completely, you can use this:

const heif_security_limits* no_limits = heif_get_disabled_security_limits();
heif_context_set_security_limits(context, no_limits);
```
Perhaps this is what IM should do? Or perhaps set the heif limit equal to IM's memory limit?

An IM developer may comment.

---
[c4] @dlemstra 2025-04-18T17:22:47Z:
Thanks for mentioning this. We had some patches in place for the security limits in heic but your comment just reminded me of a change that I had to make for this specific setting. In the next release the limit will be set to the `system:max-memory-request` that we have inside ImageMagick.
---

title: Provide command-line option to disable delegates; or, identify is extremely slow on video files
need_summary: Whether disabling delegates per command is needed to prevent code injection and untrusted input from triggering external commands, and the answer rests on the documented ImageMagick security policy and the `policy domain="delegate" rights="none" pattern="*"` example.
security_topic: per-invocation disabling of delegates vs security policy configuration
question_text: Would it be reasonable to check for a `-define` option in `delegate.c` to control the logic of `ExternalDelegateCommand`, or to make the check at any callsite using delegates?
answer_text: The security policy allows all delegates, some, or none.  If the administrator disables some or all the delegates, the user cannot enable them without administrative privileges, that is the role of the administrator, to dictate policy over their environment.  However, if the administrator wants to delegate policy decisions to the user, they can install ImageMagick with the `disable-install` option.
thread_text:
ISSUE #8038: Provide command-line option to disable delegates; or, identify is extremely slow on video files Author: Earnestly Date: 2025-03-16T15:21:51Z Labels: State: closed [c0] ### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe. When attempting to use `magick -ping "$file" -format '%[mime:type]\n' info:` on video files, such as `video/mp4`, IM will delegate to: ``` video:decode => "ffmpeg' -nostdin -loglevel error -i '%s' -an -f rawvideo -y %s '%s" ``` For large, or really even small video files, this process can take an extordinary amount of time and cpu usage. _(Note that interrupting `magick` with `Ctrl-C` does not kill the `ffmpeg` child so the process remains running, nor does it clean up `/tmp` symlinks.)_ ### Describe the solution you'd like Rather than trying to account for each delegate and their potential onerous behaviours, I would very much like the ability to disable all delegates via the command-line. I'm aware that this might be possible by either modifying `/etc/ImageMagick-7/delegates.xml` or changing the policy in `/etc/ImageMagick-7/policy.xml`, but both of these require root permissions and effect global usage of `magick` which would not be my intention. Ideally `magick` could introduce a `-define` which allows me to disable the use of delegates entirely. _(PS. I am not personally interested in using delegates and so do not need any kind of per-delegate control.)_ --- COMMENTS --- [c1] @urban-warrior 2025-03-16T15:40:08Z: Add `[0]` to your command-line to speed up video processing: ``` magick -ping "$file[0]" -format '%[mime:type]\n' info: ```` Adding a command-line option could be a security issue. By the default, ImageMagick polices are controlled by the administrator. If you perform a non-standard install, ImageMagick can instead consult your local `delegates.xml` and you can disable delegates at will by altering the default configuration. --- [c2] @snibgo 2025-03-16T15:42:08Z: > I'm aware that this might be possible by either modifying /etc/ImageMagick-7/delegates.xml or changing the policy in /etc/ImageMagick-7/policy.xml, but both of these require root permissions and effect global usage of magick which would not be my intention. You can create a `policy.xml` for individual users. This will apply further limits, on top of any imposed by the global `policy.xml`. --- [c3] @Earnestly 2025-03-16T17:23:57Z: I really do not want to create per-user policy files. I also won't be able to use `[0]` notation (hopefully) once `filename:literal=true` works for both inputs and outputs. I'm also unsure why it would be a security issue if a user is allowed to _disable_ delegates on a per-command basis. If anything, it would make imagemagick _more_ secure as delegates are just commands, resolved via `PATH`, and users have full control over that. Please consider nicely what you're suggesting. If someone wants to use `magick` in a script, just one command in many, and the author wants some guarantee that arbitrary inputs are not going to wreak havok, there is currently _no_ way to do it. Because `magick` has no way to disable delegates, and because delegates are user controlled objects, by dint this means any such script may execute arbitrary code based on carefully constructed inputs, whether it's `magick`'s own filename evaluation strategies or full execution control based on delegate. I have no idea why this behaviour should be at the sole discretion of a "system admin", as it means any script that uses `magick` now relies on a carefully controlled and sanitised execution environment. ```sh $ cat ffmpeg #!/bin/sh -- echo hi > owned $ PATH=.:$PATH magick -ping video/1917.mp4 -format '%[mime:type]\n' info: magick: insufficient image data in file `/tmp/magick-5EIzi9um6SIwIOvJRf1zJ0nd4fuEaiaD' @ error/webp.c/ReadWEBPImage/560. $ cat owned hi ``` --- [c4] @fmw42 2025-03-16T17:30:57Z: Can you explain why you cannot use [0] to restrict to the first image in the video? Do you need to do your processing command on all the images in the video? Why? --- [c5] @urban-warrior 2025-03-16T17:41:56Z: The wonderful thing about open-source, is anyone can post a patch as a pull request and the development team will review for inclusion. Have fun. --- [c6] @Earnestly 2025-03-16T17:52:00Z: > The wonderful thing about open-source, is anyone can post a patch as a pull request and the development team will review for inclusion. Have fun. Would it be reasonable to check for a `-define` option in `delegate.c` to control the logic of `ExternalDelegateCommand`, or to make the check at any callsite using delegates? --- [c7] @urban-warrior 2025-03-16T18:05:18Z: Defines would be the simplest solution for your request. However, we are not interested in supporting a define as you can already stop all delegate execution with a single security policy.: ``` ``` If possible, we try to follow the design principle of only have one way to do one thing. --- [c8] @Earnestly 2025-03-16T18:26:32Z: > Defines would be the simplest solution for your request. However, we are not interested in supporting a define as you can already stop all delegate execution with a single security policy.: > > ``` > > > ``` How does a script executing `magick` define this policy? --- [c9] @Earnestly 2025-03-16T18:40:34Z: I disagree with the reasoning that you should follow a design principle of "only have one way to do one thing" when specifically dealing with program configuration. Here "configuration" means any external file that controls the operation of the program. (Environment variables in contrast are more a form of IPC.) Exposing configuration options via the command-line is quite typical and better enables the principle of least priviledge via refinement. Consider openssh as an example of this. _As an aside, the best tools also provide encoders and decoders for all the custom datatypes it employs, typically for custom string encoding, or the capacity to query configuration data in a programmatic manner without expecting each user to implement ad-hoc parsers._ I have managed to find a reasonably sensible way to disable delegates via a `-define`, which I may provide as a PR soon: ```diff diff --git a/MagickCore/constitute.c b/MagickCore/constitute.c index 03fd3ef97..28fe55829 100644 --- a/MagickCore/constitute.c +++ b/MagickCore/constitute.c @@ -621,6 +621,9 @@ MagickExport Image *ReadImage(const ImageInfo *image_info, const MagickInfo *magick_info; + const char + *option; + DecodeImageHandler *decoder; @@ -722,7 +725,9 @@ MagickExport Image *ReadImage(const ImageInfo *image_info, decoder=GetImageDecoder(magick_info); } } - if (decoder != (DecodeImageHandler *) NULL) + option=GetImageOption(image_info,"delegates"); + if (decoder != (DecodeImageHandler *) NULL && + (IsStringTrue(option) != MagickFalse)) { /* Call appropriate image reader based on image type. diff --git a/www/defines.html b/www/defines.html index 6096710df..ceec81be4 100644 --- a/www/defines.html +++ b/www/defines.html @@ -418,6 +418,11 @@ use:

By default, an output filename can contain embedded formatting characters. Use this option to bypass interpreting embedded formatting characters and instead use the filename literally. + + delegates=true + By default allow delegates to execute according to policy. See Security. + + filter:option=value Set a filter option for use with -resize. ``` --- [c10] @fmw42 2025-03-16T18:41:42Z: > Can you explain why you cannot use [0] ... > > Because the inputs are user controlled. **This is not a very clear and understandable reason, at least for me. Please show some code so that we can understand your issue and why you cannot specify an image name.** --- [c11] @Earnestly 2025-03-16T19:20:35Z: > > Can you explain why you cannot use [0] ... > > Because the inputs are user controlled. > > **This is not a very clear and understandable reason, at least for me. Please show some code so that we can understand your issue and why you cannot specify an image name.** Oh sorry, I'll try to explain my reasoning: _For a bit of background here is a good article that covers code injection: https://www.more-magic.net/posts/structurally-fixing-injection-bugs.html_ Everything is about encoding. And a lot of it is often accidental: here accidental means that formats are used but not enforced or checked. Consider a UNIX filename consisting of an arbitrary sequence of bytes, excluding `/`, terminated by a NUL byte. In contrast a Windows filename excludes many more characters and encodes them using the USC-2, it also imparts special meanings to files with specific names. One consequence of this is that valid UNIX and Windows filenames **cannot be represented** in JSON (as it only supports UTF-8), for example. Yet people do this anyway, largely successfully (this is the accidental part). When ImageMagick parses filenames and evaluates their meaning, it has implicitly (or explicitly) created a new "encoding" for filenames, which are at variance with UNIX/Windows filenames (like JSON, but different). The problem arises when the inputs to your program, which you have no control over, uses one encoding (datatype) while the software expects another. There are generally three ways to solve this problem; one is to encode the input to the encoding the program expects, another is to ensure the software treats the input as an array of bytes and to not interpret the bytes at all. The second approach is the ideal solution as it obviates the need to "escape" or "sanitise" inputs. In other words, by never exposing user-supplied data to code evaluation, you will never suffer from code injection. However, if you cannot do that (such as interpreting image data) then you must enforce the encoding (this is what your oss-fuzz tests are doing) and ensure your parser can deal with malformed input. (cf. Weird Machines) What I am essentially asking for is a way to provide this data, un-interpreted. Consider SQL and prepared statements as analogous to my request. However if "prepared statements" are not possible (i.e. `filename:literal=true` for both input and output filenames) then I must resort to something like `safe_escape_string_for_real_this_time()`. If there is no "encoding" for imagemagick filenames, e.g. `png\:\-` as a filename vs. `png:-` as special meaning to imagemagick, then I can only detect this encoding/datatype, check it, and error out as a "type mismatch". This is the third option. _PS. A good set of examples are shell scripts which rely on word splitting that only work when file names don't contain spaces, see the myriad ways shell scripts tend to accidently practice code injection without realising: https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashProgramming/05_ Sorry if a bit long winded, but hopefully it makes my point of view a bit clearer. _PPS. Yes, this started as an issue with `ffmpeg` being slow when attempting to query file information, but once I saw `magick -list delegates` I decided that I would much rather completely disable this feature for my scripts which don't need it._ --- [c12] @fmw42 2025-03-16T19:33:47Z: Thank you. Sorry I am not a coder (I just do bash scripting), so I don't really understand the significance other than you seem to be trying to trap injection. I don't really understand why you cannot use [N] as part of the filename. Can your code for reading a filename not handle that. If not, then read the file into IM with a command that converts the file to some filename.miff, i.e. magick your_filename.suffix your_filename.miff". Then while in IM, do "magick filename.miff[0] some-processing output.suffix". Does that help in any way to solve your issue. If not, then it is over my head" --- [c13] @urban-warrior 2025-03-16T19:42:08Z: We cover the topic of security in https://imagemagick.org/script/security-policy.php and we even offer a security policy that is stringent and covers all or most of your concerns @ https://imagemagick.org/source/policy-secure.xml. Use this security policy to eliminate all paths to code injection and then add in all the other recommendations discussed in the security policy page to ensure ImageMagick is maximally secure. As mentioned, ImageMagick is open source, and we encourage users to patch the source distributions to match their requirements and install in their environment. --- [c14] @Earnestly 2025-03-16T20:00:02Z: @fmw42 > Thank you. Sorry I am not a coder (I just do bash scripting), No problem, bash scripting is probably one of the places this "problem of encoding" shows up the most because many of the scripts involve [marshalling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshalling_(computer_science)) data between programs (i.e. everytime you send data over a \ `|`, you are implicitly encoding and decoding data). See the link at the bottom of my last reply for a nice list of surprising places were arbitrary code execution is possible. I also want to clarify that most cases of arbitrary code execution (ACE) are not malicious, it's often unintentional, surfacing as bugs or wonky edge cases that cause a bit of confusion for awhile. This is a class of bugs you will want to avoid even if not for the "security" aspects. > I don't really understand why you cannot use [N] as part of the filename. The problem isn't that I cannot use `[N]` but that a user might provide a filename containing those characters. And instead of the filename being interpreted as a filename, it is parsed and evaluated as an imagemagick filename. Does this make sense? > Can your code for reading a filename not handle that. I can hopefully demonstrate a session: ```sh $ magick 'foo.gif[0]' -format '%[mime:type]' info: image/gif% $ cp foo.gif 'bar.gif[0]' 'foo.gif' -> 'bar.gif[0]' $ file --mime-type 'bar.gif[0]' bar.gif[0]: image/gif $ magick 'bar.gif[0]' -format '%[mime:type]' info: image/gifimage/gifimage/gifimage/gifimage/gifimage/gifimage/gifimage/gifimage/gifimage/gifimage/gifimage/gifimage/gif $ magick 'bar.gif[0][0]' -format '%[mime:type]' info: magick: no decode delegate for this image format `' @ error/constitute.c/ReadImage/746. ``` > If not, then read the file into IM with a command that converts the file to some filename.miff, i.e. magick your_filename.suffix your_filename.miff". Then while in IM, do "magick filename.miff[0] some-processing output.suffix". Does that help in any way to solve your issue. If not, then it is over my head This is actually quite a nice suggestion. I could normalise the input filename using a symbolic link, then operate on the symbolic link instead of the given name. Although less than optimal because now it means creating a symlink somewhere and it introduces race conditions if the script is executed in parallel, which would then require some kind of unique naming scheme using tools like `mktemp` (not yet POSIX); despite this however, it would solve the problem of `filename:literal=true` not applying to the input filename. ```sh $ ln -s 'bar.gif[0]' norm 'norm' -> 'bar.gif[0]' $ magick 'norm[0]' -format '%[mime:type]' info: image/gif ``` Thank you for the idea, I didn't consider normalisation for the filenames. --- [c15] @Earnestly 2025-03-16T20:18:30Z: @urban-warrior > We cover the topic of security in https://imagemagick.org/script/security-policy.php and we even offer a security policy that is stringent and covers all or most of your concerns @ https://imagemagick.org/source/policy-secure.xml. Use this security policy to eliminate all paths to code injection and then add in all the other recommendations discussed in the security policy page to ensure ImageMagick is maximally secure. But I do not control distro policy or have root access to every user's machine to adjust their policy documents. You wouldn't require `ssh` users to edit the root owned `/etc/ssh/ssh_config` file just use `ProxyJump` for one particular invocation. Additionally why should all distributions cater to my requirements? Or why should other users on the same system be subject to _my_ policy choices? Consider forcing everyone who uses a particular distribution, or those on a particular machine, to use `-alpha on` because my one of my scripts required it. This doesn't make any sense to me. > As mentioned, ImageMagick is open source, and we encourage users to patch the source distributions to match their requirements and install in their environment. You have already written that what I want will not be accepted and I do not think any reasonable distribution will deviate from upstream because of a niche configuration change (nor should they). --- [c16] @urban-warrior 2025-03-16T20:26:37Z: The administrator has full control over the machine, allowing them to decide how ImageMagick should operate in their environment. This approach is commonly adopted on both Linux and Windows hosts. Alternatively, the administrator may choose to install ImageMagick using the "no-install" option. By doing so, they delegate the responsibility for configuration to the user. In such cases, the user gains the flexibility to override the system's delegate, security policies, and other settings by creating a custom configuration within their home directory. Another viable option for users is to build a personalized instance of ImageMagick directly in their home directory, granting them complete freedom to modify the configuration files as needed. --- [c17] @Earnestly 2025-03-16T20:49:52Z: @urban-warrior > This approach is commonly adopted on both Linux If by "this" you mean not allowing configuration control through command-line options, then it is not particularly true of Linux. I can't speak to Windows. Even the lowely `ulimit` allows users to reduce (not increase) various hard and soft limits, nevermind tools like `nginx -g ` or `git -c`. > Alternatively, the administrator may choose to install ImageMagick using the "no-install" option. Scripts cannot depend on administrators installing tools in special ways. Just as a user cannot depend on an administrator installing `/etc/ssh/ssh_config` with their specific `ProxyJump` destination address set correctly for their specific needs at a specific moment in time. > By doing so, they delegate the responsibility for configuration to the user. comments.author: Earnestly
comments.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

When attempting to use `magick -ping "$file" -format '%[mime:type]\n' info:` on video files, such as `video/mp4`, IM will delegate to:

```
video:decode =>          "ffmpeg' -nostdin -loglevel error -i '%s' -an -f rawvideo -y %s '%s"
```

For large, or really even small video files, this process can take an extordinary amount of time and cpu usage.

_(Note that interrupting `magick` with `Ctrl-C` does not kill the `ffmpeg` child so the process remains running, nor does it clean up `/tmp` symlinks.)_


### Describe the solution you'd like

Rather than trying to account for each delegate and their potential onerous behaviours, I would very much like the ability to disable all delegates via the command-line.

I'm aware that this might be possible by either modifying `/etc/ImageMagick-7/delegates.xml` or changing the policy in `/etc/ImageMagick-7/policy.xml`, but both of these require root permissions and effect global usage of `magick` which would not be my intention.

Ideally `magick` could introduce a `-define` which allows me to disable the use of delegates entirely.

_(PS. I am not personally interested in using delegates and so do not need any kind of per-delegate control.)_

comments.author: urban-warrior
comments.body:
Add `[0]` to your command-line to speed up video processing:

```
magick -ping "$file[0]" -format '%[mime:type]\n' info:
````

Adding a command-line option could be a security issue.  By the default, ImageMagick polices are controlled by the administrator.  If you perform a non-standard install, ImageMagick can instead consult your local `delegates.xml` and you can disable delegates at will by altering the default configuration.

I disagree with the reasoning that you should follow a design principle of "only have one way to do one thing" when specifically dealing with program configuration. Here "configuration" means any external file that controls the operation of the program. (Environment variables in contrast are more a form of IPC.) Exposing configuration options via the command-line is quite typical and better enables the principle of least priviledge via refinement. Consider openssh as an example of this. _As an aside, the best tools also provide encoders and decoders for all the custom datatypes it employs, typically for custom string encoding, or the capacity to query configuration data in a programmatic manner without expecting each user to implement ad-hoc parsers._ I have managed to find a reasonably sensible way to disable delegates via a `-define`, which I may provide as a PR soon: ```diff diff --git a/MagickCore/constitute.c b/MagickCore/constitute.c index 03fd3ef97..28fe55829 100644 --- a/MagickCore/constitute.c +++ b/MagickCore/constitute.c @@ -621,6 +621,9 @@ MagickExport Image *ReadImage(const ImageInfo *image_info, const MagickInfo *magick_info; + const char + *option; + DecodeImageHandler *decoder; @@ -722,7 +725,9 @@ MagickExport Image *ReadImage(const ImageInfo *image_info, decoder=GetImageDecoder(magick_info); } } - if (decoder != (DecodeImageHandler *) NULL) + option=GetImageOption(image_info,"delegates"); + if (decoder != (DecodeImageHandler *) NULL && + (IsStringTrue(option) != MagickFalse)) { /* Call appropriate image reader based on image type. diff --git a/www/defines.html b/www/defines.html index 6096710df..ceec81be4 100644 --- a/www/defines.html +++ b/www/defines.html @@ -418,6 +418,11 @@ use:

By default, an output filename can contain embedded formatting characters. Use this option to bypass interpreting embedded formatting characters and instead use the filename literally. + + delegates=true + By default allow delegates to execute according to policy. See Security. + + filter:option=value Set a filter option for use with -resize. ```

comments.body:
> > Can you explain why you cannot use [0] ...
> > Because the inputs are user controlled.
> 
> **This is not a very clear and understandable reason, at least for me. Please show some code so that we can understand your issue and why you cannot specify an image name.**

Oh sorry, I'll try to explain my reasoning:

_For a bit of background here is a good article that covers code injection: https://www.more-magic.net/posts/structurally-fixing-injection-bugs.html_

Everything is about encoding. And a lot of it is often accidental: here accidental means that formats are used but not enforced or checked.

Consider a UNIX filename consisting of an arbitrary sequence of bytes, excluding `/`, terminated by a NUL byte. In contrast a Windows filename excludes many more characters and encodes them using the USC-2, it also imparts special meanings to files with specific names.

One consequence of this is that valid UNIX and Windows filenames **cannot be represented** in JSON (as it only supports UTF-8), for example. Yet people do this anyway, largely successfully (this is the accidental part).

When ImageMagick parses filenames and evaluates their meaning, it has implicitly (or explicitly) created a new "encoding" for filenames, which are at variance with UNIX/Windows filenames (like JSON, but different).

The problem arises when the inputs to your program, which you have no control over, uses one encoding (datatype) while the software expects another. There are generally three ways to solve this problem; one is to encode the input to the encoding the program expects, another is to ensure the software treats the input as an array of bytes and to not interpret the bytes at all. The second approach is the ideal solution as it obviates the need to "escape" or "sanitise" inputs.

In other words, by never exposing user-supplied data to code evaluation, you will never suffer from code injection. However, if you cannot do that (such as interpreting image data) then you must enforce the encoding (this is what your oss-fuzz tests are doing) and ensure your parser can deal with malformed input. (cf. Weird Machines)

What I am essentially asking for is a way to provide this data, un-interpreted. Consider SQL and prepared statements as analogous to my request. However if "prepared statements" are not possible (i.e. `filename:literal=true` for both input and output filenames) then I must resort to something like `safe_escape_string_for_real_this_time()`.

If there is no "encoding" for imagemagick filenames, e.g. `png\:\-` as a filename vs. `png:-` as special meaning to imagemagick, then I can only detect this encoding/datatype, check it, and error out as a "type mismatch". This is the third option.

_PS. A good set of examples are shell scripts which rely on word splitting that only work when file names don't contain spaces, see the myriad ways shell scripts tend to accidently practice code injection without realising: https://mywiki.wooledge.org/BashProgramming/05_

Sorry if a bit long winded, but hopefully it makes my point of view a bit clearer.

_PPS. Yes, this started as an issue with `ffmpeg` being slow when attempting to query file information, but once I saw `magick -list delegates` I decided that I would much rather completely disable this feature for my scripts which don't need it._

title: JXL->JXL processing (to remove alpha channel) drops color profile
need_summary: Whether ImageMagick’s JXL encoder is dropping the original ICC profile because it always calls JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding instead of JXLEncoderSetICCProfile, as discussed in libjxl’s encoder docs and the linked source snippet test_utils.cc#L792.
security_topic: ICC profile loss when converting JXL while removing alpha
question_text: The image no longer has an alpha channel (that's good!), but has lost the ICC profile and other metadata.
answer_text:
The delegate's `WriteJXLImage()` _always_ calls `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` (via `JXLWriteMetadata()`)... but the docs for that function clearly say that only one of `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` or `JXLEncoderSetICCProfile()` can be used.

The delegate never calls `JXLEncoderSetICCProfile()` currently, and even if it did that would be invalid, because it's still going to unconditionally call `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()`.

...It **will** attempt to preserve any EXIF or XMP metadata by applying it to the output image with `JXLEncoderAddBox()`, but that doesn't help if the profile _isn't in_ an EXIF or XMP blob (like when it comes from a JXL input file, but possibly also via a PNG `iCCP` chunk or other non-EXIF/XMP source)... and from what @jonnyawsom3 says about the overrides I'm not sure profiles from those metadata blobs would be used either, if `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` is still called.

The delegate is treating `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` as essential, required metadata that must always be set on an image to be encoded. But from what I can tell based on the documentation and @jonnyawsom3 's comments, nothing could be further from the truth, and it should ONLY be used when explicitly _not_ applying an ICC profile.

[c11] @ferdnyc 2025-03-28T01:20:54Z:
I was going to close this in favor of libjxl/libjxl#4164, because my inability to apply the same color profile using the `cjxl` encoder makes me suspect this is a libjxl bug more than an ImageMagick bug.

---
[c12] @jonnyawsom3 2025-03-29T10:34:01Z:
I said it on the libjxl issue, but lossy encoding stores color space Enums (stripped down versions of common color spaces like sRGB, Rec2020, P3, ect) instead of the original ICC. This may help figure out what needs to be changed https://github.com/libjxl/libjxl/blob/0c1aba1d51ed32f61be4de638f075f2b199082d0/lib/jxl/test_utils.cc#L792

[c13] @ferdnyc 2025-03-30T05:17:37Z:
Thanks @jonnyawsom3 

I see the issue now. The delegate's `WriteJXLImage()` _always_ calls `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` (via `JXLWriteMetadata()`)... but the docs for that function clearly say that only one of `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` or `JXLEncoderSetICCProfile()` can be used.

The delegate never calls `JXLEncoderSetICCProfile()` currently, and even if it did that would be invalid, because it's still going to unconditionally call `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()`.

...It **will** attempt to preserve any EXIF or XMP metadata by applying it to the output image with `JXLEncoderAddBox()`, but that doesn't help if the profile _isn't in_ an EXIF or XMP blob (like when it comes from a JXL input file, but possibly also via a PNG `iCCP` chunk or other non-EXIF/XMP source)... and from what @jonnyawsom3 says about the overrides I'm not sure profiles from those metadata blobs would be used either, if `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` is still called.

The delegate is treating `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` as essential, required metadata that must always be set on an image to be encoded. But from what I can tell based on the documentation and @jonnyawsom3 's comments, nothing could be further from the truth, and it should ONLY be used when explicitly _not_ applying an ICC profile.
---
[c14] @ferdnyc 2025-03-30T05:30:35Z:
Heh. The delegate's encode function even does this:

```c
  if (image_info->quality == 100)
    basic_info.uses_original_profile=JXL_TRUE;
```

...But then makes a liar out of itself by never calling `JXLEncoderSetICCProfile()` to attach the original color profile that it's telling the decoder it's supposed to use.

(I think the assumption might have been that this tells the _encoder_ to use the original profile... but IIUC from the docs, it's actually just a flag for the _decoder_ that tells it how to decode the JXL file that's output by the encoder. If the profile doesn't get attached to that output, the flag doesn't really mean anything.)
---
[c15] @jonnyawsom3 2025-03-30T10:25:48Z:
Close, but the naming is throwing you off like many before. `basic_info.uses_original_profile` actually controls the internal color space, XYB for lossy and RGB for lossless. Libjxl will throw an error if you try to do lossless XYB.

I think you're right about SetICC and SetColorEncoding though. 
---

comments.body:
I was going to close this in favor of libjxl/libjxl#4164, because my inability to apply the same color profile using the `cjxl` encoder makes me suspect this is a libjxl bug more than an ImageMagick bug.

However, the jury isn't COMPLETELY in on that. Because:

1. I can use `djxl` and `cjxl` to convert the original file through JPEG (JXL->JPG->JXL), and the profile will be preserved at each step.
2. When I use ImageMagick to do the same thing, the profile survives the JXL->JPG conversion, but is again lost in the JPG->JXL conversion.

So, there may indeed be issues with ImageMagick's JXL encoding not preserving color profile metadata in situations where the JXL reference tools would.

comments.author: jonnyawsom3
comments.body:
I said it on the libjxl issue, but lossy encoding stores color space Enums (stripped down versions of common color spaces like sRGB, Rec2020, P3, ect) instead of the original ICC. It seems ImageMagick is allowing libjxl to use the Enums for lossless too. It shouldn't have a noticeable visual impact, but it's not truly lossless either.

This may help figure out what needs to be changed https://github.com/libjxl/libjxl/blob/0c1aba1d51ed32f61be4de638f075f2b199082d0/lib/jxl/test_utils.cc#L792

comments.author: ferdnyc
comments.body:
Thanks @jonnyawsom3 

I see the issue now. The delegate's `WriteJXLImage()` _always_ calls `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` (via `JXLWriteMetadata()`)... but the docs for that function clearly say that only one of `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` or `JXLEncoderSetICCProfile()` can be used.

The delegate never calls `JXLEncoderSetICCProfile()` currently, and even if it did that would be invalid, because it's still going to unconditionally call `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()`.

...It **will** attempt to preserve any EXIF or XMP metadata by applying it to the output image with `JXLEncoderAddBox()`, but that doesn't help if the profile _isn't in_ an EXIF or XMP blob (like when it comes from a JXL input file, but possibly also via a PNG `iCCP` chunk or other non-EXIF/XMP source)... and from what @jonnyawsom3 says about the overrides I'm not sure profiles from those metadata blobs would be used either, if `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` is still called.

The delegate is treating `JXLEncoderSetColorEncoding()` as essential, required metadata that must always be set on an image to be encoded. But from what I can tell based on the documentation and @jonnyawsom3 's comments, nothing could be further from the truth, and it should ONLY be used when explicitly _not_ applying an ICC profile.

comments.author: ferdnyc
comments.body:
Heh. The delegate's encode function even does this:

```c
  if (image_info->quality == 100)
    basic_info.uses_original_profile=JXL_TRUE;
```

...But then makes a liar out of itself by never calling `JXLEncoderSetICCProfile()` to attach the original color profile that it's telling the decoder it's supposed to use.

(I think the assumption might have been that this tells the _encoder_ to use the original profile... but IIUC from the docs, it's actually just a flag for the _decoder_ that tells it how to decode the JXL file that's output by the encoder. If the profile doesn't get attached to that output, the flag doesn't really mean anything.)

comments.author: jonnyawsom3
comments.body:
Close, but the naming is throwing you off like many before. `basic_info.uses_original_profile` actually controls the internal color space, XYB for lossy and RGB for lossless. Libjxl will throw an error if you try to do lossless XYB.

I think you're right about SetICC and SetColorEncoding though.

title: Fax and Group4 pdf to tiff compression not working in 7.1.1.44
need_summary: Whether Fax/Group4 TIFF compression is silently skipped for PDF-derived images because Ghostscript renders them with an alpha channel, and the answer rests on commit 2f6593a4ef90e25475923ce0e4be1bd37036ebcc plus the documented Ghostscript delegate/pngalpha behavior.
security_topic: Fax/Group4 compression failure triggered by alpha channel in PDF rendering
question_text:
I'm on arch linux trying to convert a pdf scan to 1-bit tiff (bueracratic requirement) with a sane filesize. I used to do Fax compression for this purpose, but it stopped working. Funnily enough, converting from jpeg or png to tiff correctly produces an image with the desired compression. The issue seems to be specific to pdf->tiff conversion only. EDIT: wrong, i forgot to revert to V44. It doesn't compress with other conversions too. EDIT2: apparently it's the alpha. Jpegs work fine, so do RGB PNGs. PDFs and RGBA PNGs break.

I do `magick -density 300 input.pdf -depth 1 -compress Fax output.tiff`
The resulting image is an 1mb uncompressed tiff (identified by `magick identify -verbose` saying `Compression: None`) to 400kb source PDF scan (jpeg inside).

Trying `-compress Group4` gives the same result.

Rolling back to 7.1.1.43 fixes the issue
answer_text: We leverage the Ghostscript delegate to render PDF and the default device is `pngalpha` which renders the alpha channel.  You can instead change the device in `delegates.xml` to `png16m` to render PDF/PS without transparency.

We leverage the Ghostscript delegate to render PDF and the default device is `pngalpha` which renders the alpha channel.  You can instead change the device in `delegates.xml` to `png16m` to render PDF/PS without transparency.

Well, the input.pdf in question was generated by imagemagick itstelf from a JPEG image. The source had no alpha. In fact I just tried to info: several PDFs of different nature - a Kyocera scan, an image converted to PDF with imagemagick (also with `-alpha off`), an open office document with no images (`pdfimages -list` shows empty) saved to PDF. They all show alpha preseent. Apparently you can't have PDF without alpha.

This means if you want to get a compressed tiff from any PDF, you must specify `-alpha off`, but it's black magic that can only be known by looking at the source code. If you don't do it, you silently get an uncompressed tiff for entirely unknown and unknowable reason. There is no meaningful difference between `-alpha on` and `-alpha off` results observable with exiftool or mediainfo or magick identify - there's no mention of alpha in any of them. 

In fact I just experimented with an actual transparent PNG source. `magick input.png output.tiff` produces an image with 4 channels. `magick input.png -alpha off output.tiff` produces an image with 3 channels. `magick input.png -compress Fax output.tiff` produces an image with 1 1-bit channel. It still removes all the channels, just doesn't do compression. Silently.   

From a user perspective this looks like Fax compression just not working. 

If the intended behaviour is to prevent compression of sources containing an alpha channel, there probably should be a warning or a failure. As it is, it does one half of the job (converting image to 1 channel 1-bit black and white) and silently omits the other half of the job. It's impossible to tell why you aren't getting the result you want.

comments.author: urban-warrior
comments.body: We leverage the Ghostscript delegate to render PDF and the default device is `pngalpha` which renders the alpha channel.  You can instead change the device in `delegates.xml` to `png16m` to render PDF/PS without transparency.

comments.author: emk2203
comments.body:
For anyone arriving here via Google and in search of a broader solution:

[This comment on Stackoverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10934456/imagemagick-pdf-to-jpgs-sometimes-results-in-black-background#comment99113684_16293489) gives a better approach.

>I am converting PDF to TIFF (for faxing) and was using "-alpha off" by default, but would see all black pages if the page had PDF form fields or signatures pasted in as transparent PNG's. Changing to "-alpha remove" worked as florian suggests. I played with other alpha values but remove is the way to go.

To avoid most issues, `magick -density 300 input.pdf -compress Fax -alpha remove -background white output.tiff` is recommended.

title: ImageMagick Incorrectly Handles Negative biHeight for Compressed Formats
need_summary: Whether ImageMagick should reject BMP files with negative biHeight for compressed formats, based on the Microsoft BITMAPINFOHEADER specification and the maintainer’s patch response.
security_topic: BMP parser validation for negative biHeight in compressed formats
question_text:
I would like to report an observation regarding ImageMagick's handling of BMP files with compressed formats.

 According to the Microsoft documentation for the `BITMAPINFOHEADER` structure, the `biHeight` field **must be positive for compressed formats**, regardless of image orientation. However, I found that ImageMagick can still parse and process BMP files with negative `biHeight` values for compressed formats without any warnings or errors.

You can expect this patch to be merged into the [main GIT branch](https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick), later today. --- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @fmw42 2025-02-19T16:17:51Z:
On my Mac OSX Ventura with Inkscape 1.3.2_4 installed as the SVG renderer in Imagemagick 7.1.1.43 , I get

```
magick test.svg x.png

** (<unknown>:1149): WARNING **: 08:10:08.852: attribute 'clip-path' given as CSS

(<unknown>:1149): glibmm-WARNING **: 08:10:08.866: Failed to wrap object of type 'GtkRecentManager'. Hint: this error is commonly caused by failing to call a library init() function.
```

However, the PNG output is generated.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e531cc4-2dbe-48b1-8ac7-c3a80dc84a17)


You should use Inkscape as the best of the following 3 renderers.

What is your SVG renderer (Inkscape if installed on your system, RSVG delegate if installed in IM or the default internal MSVG/XML renderer)?

You can find out for the latter two if used by the following command. (However, Inkscape will be used over the other two when installed on your system)

magick -list format

then find the line for SVG and at the end it will tell you what is installed.

For Inkscape, use

`inkscape --version`

For all of them, just add -verbose after magick in the command 

`magick -verbose test.svg x.png`

Yes, it appears that you only have the internal XML renderer which is the worst of the 3.  Install Inkscape on your system where it can be found by Imagemagick (make sure it is in your $PATH environment variable). Then try again.

How did you determine that Inkscape was not there?  Did you use

`Inkscape --version`

to check?

title: identify: no decode delegate for this image format `HEIC' @ error/constitute.c/ReadImage/746.
need_summary: Whether HEIC support was missing because Fedora also needs the ImageMagick-heic package and, for newer iPhone files, libheif >= 1.18.x as noted in the linked Fedora bugzilla report.
security_topic: HEIC decode support and library/version compatibility
question_text: Any idea as to how can I solve it?
answer_text:
On Fedora you need to also install `ImageMagick-heic`, only then would it show up in the format list?

Also, if the HEIC images are from a more recent iPhone (iOS 18), you need libheif >= 1.18.x, which is [not yet available in Fedora](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2332519) (will be in F42).

title: Crash when opening some exr files
need_summary: Whether a malformed OpenEXR file can crash ImageMagick during decoding, and the maintainer says a patch was pushed to fix it for the next release.
security_topic: crash on decoding malformed EXR files
question_text:
Some EXR files will cause magick (amongst other things) to crash when they are decoded.

This looks like it's due to an issue in the underlying openexr library coming up with no channels, but there's an assumption that there is at least one channel in `exr.c` in the function `InitializeEXRChannels` where the channel name prefix is checked
answer_text: Thanks for reporting this. I just pushed a patch that fixes this issue. This will be resolved in the next release.

Author: mrsneeze

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

7.1.1-43

### Operating system

Windows

### Operating system, version and so on

10

### Description

Some EXR files will cause magick (amongst other things) to crash when they are decoded.

This looks like it's due to an issue in the underlying openexr library coming up with no channels, but there's an assumption that there is at least one channel in `exr.c` in the function `InitializeEXRChannels` where the channel name prefix is checked

### Steps to Reproduce

`magick Kapaa.exr out.jpg`

This will cause magick.exe to crash.

I think IM only supports the half format (16-bits). Is this the full format?  An IM developer will need to comment. further.

I can open it in GraphicConverter on my Mac.  

`ExifTool says it is EXR Version: 2` 

```

need_summary: Whether the HTTP image-reading capability was broken by removed libxml2 methods and would be restored in the next release, per the maintainer’s patch note in comment c5.
security_topic: HTTP URL decoding regression in ImageMagick
question_text:
trying to convert an image from an http address results in the following error:
`magick: no decode delegate for this image format 'HTTP' @ error/constitute.c/ReadImage/746.`

doing the same in version 7.1.1-41 and earlier works as expected.

running `magick -list format` on 7.1.1-43 results in:
`HTTP* URL       ---   Uniform Resource Locator (http://)`

using the same command on 7.1.1-41 results in:
`HTTP* URL       r--   Uniform Resource Locator (http://)`

is there a way to make the format readable again?
answer_text: I could not reproduce this on Windows so I incorrectly assumed it must be something in the build but it turns out this is happening because some libxml2 methods were removed in the non Windows builds. I just pushed a patch to restore support for this in a different way and that will become available in the next release.

title: Converting some images to PICT results in files that will crash a classic Mac system
need_summary: Whether ImageMagick’s PICT encoder is producing malformed files that crash classic Mac OS, and the answer rests on the cited Inside Macintosh: Volume V documentation plus the specific ImageMagick source lines in pict.c that should compare `bytes_per_line > 250`.
security_topic: PICT file format validity causing classic Mac OS crash
question_text: Converting certain images to a PICT file will produce files that will crash the system when attempting to view them on a classic Mac OS system. I've reproduced the crash on Macintosh System 7.1, Mac OS 8, and Mac OS 9.
answer_text: I do believe I found the issue. The key is in page 119 of Inside Macintosh: Volume V, where it describes how the pixel data of a PICT should be written out. Here's a screen shot of the relevant section: The key part is where it says "If rowBytes > 250". In `bad.pict`, rowBytes is 240, but the `byteCount` of each scanline is two bytes rather than one. I just manually modified the file so that the `byteCount` entries for each scanline is only one byte, and it fixed the file, in that classic Mac OS can now properly read it. (See : [fixed.pict.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18159393/fixed.pict.zip) ) This bug apparently affects ImageMagick's PICT reader as well, as it's unable to open `fixed.pict` and produces this error: error/pict.c/ReadPICTImage/1267. In fact, I think that points me to the error, see: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/blob/b77eb776838b6039834948bb63f8106a7980554b/coders/pict.c#L504 That should be: if (bytes_per_line > 250) Same here: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/blob/b77eb776838b6039834948bb63f8106a7980554b/coders/pict.c#L694 And here too: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/blob/b77eb776838b6039834948bb63f8106a7980554b/coders/pict.c#L1087

comments.author: briankendall
comments.body:
### ImageMagick version

7.1.1-34

### Operating system

MacOS

### Operating system, version and so on

macOS 13.6.5

### Description

Converting certain images to a PICT file will produce files that will crash the system when attempting to view them on a classic Mac OS system. I've reproduced the crash on Macintosh System 7.1, Mac OS 8, and Mac OS 9.

Converting the PICT file back to a png using ImageMagick does not present any issues. I have not yet identified a modern app that presents a problem viewing the bad PICT file ImageMagick produces.

I've attached both the png file that exhibits this bug and the resulting PICT file that will crash a classic Mac.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Convert the attached png file to a pict with the following:
    `magick bad.png bad.pict`
2. Copy `bad.pict` to a system running classic Mac OS and open it in any application that can view PICT files (such as SimpleText)
3. System freezes or displays a system error

### Images

![bad](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b782b586-90d3-40fc-bde1-8438975e597d)
[bad.pict.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18142059/bad.pict.zip)

comments.author: briankendall
comments.body:
> Perhaps Apple changed the PICT format between old classic Mac and newer OSX versions.

I don't believe that's the case. The latest PICT format is "Extended Version 2" which has been around since at least the 1990s, and which is what ImageMagick is producing based off of the version information in the outputted file.

comments.author: briankendall
comments.body:
SimpleText uses the same system-level API to display a PICT as every other app in classic Mac OS. I can trigger the crash using any application that can read PICT files.

It's possible that their implementation has a bug that would cause it to crash reading an otherwise valid PICT, but I think that's unlikely. Also, given that Apple's PICT implementation from classic Mac OS is essentially the canonical implementation, I think we need to assume that ImageMagick is producing invalid files.

In fact, I think that points me to the error, see: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/blob/b77eb776838b6039834948bb63f8106a7980554b/coders/pict.c#L504 That should be: if (bytes_per_line > 250) Same here: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/blob/b77eb776838b6039834948bb63f8106a7980554b/coders/pict.c#L694 And here too: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/blob/b77eb776838b6039834948bb63f8106a7980554b/coders/pict.c#L1087

title: MNG file consumes all RAM
need_summary: Whether the MNG file-induced RAM exhaustion is a security-relevant denial-of-service issue and the answer rests on the maintainer’s policy.xml guidance to cap `list-length` because the file sets a ridiculous `LOOP` value that would otherwise create 2147483647 images.
security_topic: resource exhaustion from malformed MNG file parsing
question_text: Running `magick identify _7AD4C6FDA1664599A5DE1A7FF89000C2` on the MNG file included in the attached zip causes magick to consume all system RAM until crash.
answer_text: You should add `<policy domain="resource" name="list-length" value=""/>` to your policy.xml file and set the value to the maximum number of images that you want. Your input file contains a ridiculous `LOOP` value and that is why it's trying to create `2147483647` images.

comments.body:
Thank you for the quick response. I agree regarding the multiple memory leaks.

I'd like to point out that the `static ssize_t parse8BIM(Image ifile, Image ofile)` function also needs to be patched. Even though `static ssize_t parse8BIMW(Image ifile, Image ofile)` has been patched, memory leaks still persist in the `parse8BIM` function.

title: Inconsistent results converting between color profiles, notably involving the Lab color space
need_summary: Whether the Lab ICC profile round-trip bug in ImageMagick’s `-profile` handling was real and what patch fixed it, as confirmed by the maintainer and the follow-up patch note.
security_topic: correctness of Lab color-profile handling with ICC profiles
question_text: What is going on with the L-a-b colorspace and why is it dependent on the `-separate`  and `-combine` options? I no longer see consistency in the results with either method.
answer_text: There should be no need to translate the profile, as such we consider this a bug.  We'll add a patch to the main branch later today.  Thanks.
thread_text:
ISSUE #7724: Inconsistent results converting between color profiles, notably involving the Lab color space
Author: bosonspace
Date: 2024-10-26T12:29:32Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

7.1.1-38 Q16-HDRI x86_64 22398

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system, version and so on

Fedora 39

### Description

Since many years I have used options -colorspace and -profile to convert between colorspaces without issues. Recently I have discovered that neither of these methods give expected results when used together with the L-a-b colorspace. IM7 seems to have had major updates to color profile management, and the following behaviour is most likely a bug, or what am I otherwise doing wrong? I always avoid mixing the two options since it can create uncertainties in the color profile interpretation by IM as documented.

The Lab.icc profile has not changed on my Fedora distro and has been working fine a long long time until some recent updates to ImageMagick.

What is going on with the L-a-b colorspace and why is it dependent on the `-separate`  and `-combine` options? I no longer see consistency in the results with either method.

I have turned off color mangement for both display and image viewer when experimenting.

### Steps to Reproduce

Steps to reproduce problem using `-colorspace` method:

1:
`magick rose: -set colorspace sRGB -colorspace LAB -separate -combine -write rose1-Lab.jpg -colorspace sRGB rose1-Lab-sRGB.jpg`

The above produces a rose1-Lab.jpg which is different to original rose image as is expected. (rose1-Lab.jpg is expected to be with false colors as a result of converting pixel values to represent the LAB colorspace in each of the RGB channels). 

However, quite unexpectedly rose1-Lab-sRGB.jpg looks the same as rose1-Lab.jpg. (rose1-Lab-sRGB.jpg is expected to be in true colors and an exact copy of the original rose image as a result of pixel values being converted back to the sRGB colorspace).

![rose-Lab](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/387ef82b-20bc-4516-92f0-a52fe208a115)

2:
`magick rose: -set colorspace sRGB -colorspace LAB -write rose2-Lab.jpg -colorspace sRGB rose2-Lab-sRGB.jpg`

When removing the `-separate` and -`combine` options both rose2-Lab.jpg and rose2-sRGB.jpg remain the same as the original rose image. (rose2-Lab.jpg is appearently not in the expected LAB colorspace as previously, while rose2-Lab-sRGB.jpg is, as expected, in the same sRGB colorspace just as the original rose image).  

The same unexpected result is produced in both cases when stripping any embedded color profiles using `-strip` as first option or if skipping the first option `-set colorspace sRGB`. 

Why is the result different between using options ` -separate -combine`? Should not these two options after eachother simply cancel out?

3-4:
```
magick rose: -set colorspace sRGB -colorspace RGB -separate -combine -write rose1-RGB.jpg -colorspace sRGB rose1-RGB-sRGB.jpg
magick rose: -set colorspace sRGB -colorspace RGB -write rose2-RGB.jpg -colorspace sRGB rose2-RGB-sRGB.jpg
```

![rose-RGB](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a843ce9-4fe2-45e7-8ed7-5d0054061061)

If replacing the LAB colorspace with RGB (or sRGB) as in the above examples, then rose1-RGB.jpg and rose2-RGB.jpg are produced as expected (no matter the presence of ` -separate -combine`). However, why does not rose1-RGB-sRGB.jpg look the same as the original rose, just like rose2-RGB-sRGB.jpg does? 

Steps to reproduce problem using `-profile` method:

5-6:
```
magick rose: -profile /usr/share/color/icc/sRGB.icc -profile /usr/share/color/icc/lcms/Lab.icc -separate -combine -write rose-profile1-Lab.jpg -profile /usr/share/color/icc/sRGB.icc rose-profile1-Lab-sRGB.jpg  
magick rose: -profile /usr/share/color/icc/sRGB.icc -profile /usr/share/color/icc/lcms/Lab.icc -write rose-profile2-Lab.jpg -profile /usr/share/color/icc/sRGB.icc rose-profile2-Lab-sRGB.jpg
```  

![rose-profile-Lab](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06555df6-513d-4736-9dfc-74d9b7468e5e)

Same problem here with option `-profile` as with option `-colorspace`, but with rose-profile1-Lab.jpg being clearly redish instead of green-bluish. Why are not rose-profile1-Lab-sRGB.jpg and rose-profile2-Lab-sRGB.jpg converted back to look like the original rose? There's also here a difference between when using  `-separate -combine` or leaving it out.

In addition, although created with two different methods I would expect roseX-Lab.jpg and rose-profileX-Lab.jpg to be far more similar to each other being both in the Lab colorspace.


### Images

[color-profiles.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17530586/color-profiles.zip)


--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @snibgo 2024-10-26T13:50:14Z:
Your first command is:
```
magick rose: -set colorspace sRGB -colorspace LAB -separate -combine -write rose1-Lab.jpg -colorspace sRGB rose1-Lab-sRGB.jpg
```
> The above produces a rose1-Lab.jpg which is different to original rose image as is expected.

Yes. If you insert "`-write info:`" after "`-combine`", you will see that the image is at that point encoded as sRGB. But the pixel values are incorrect, of course.

(EDIT: Corrected "`-write info`" to "`-write info:`". It needs the colon.)

> However, quite unexpectedly rose1-Lab-sRGB.jpg looks the same as rose1-Lab.jpg.

This is expected. The image is encoded as sRGB, so "`-colorspace sRGB`" has no effect.

I think you misunderstand `-separate` and `-combine`. `-separate` replaces the current image, making one grayscale image per colour channel. The metadata describing the original colorspace is lost. `-combine` replaces the grayscale images with one colour image, and assumes the graycale images are sRGB channels. If they are not (as in your case) you should either use "`+combine Lab`", or "`-set colorspace Lab`" after the combine.

See https://imagemagick.org/script/command-line-options.php#combine

> Why is the result different between using options "-separate -combine"? Should not these two options after each other simply cancel out?

Those two together have no effect on pixel values. But they will change the colorspace metadata to sRGB.

Does that explain the problems?

The following sequence ...
```
-set option:COLSP %[colorspace] -separate +combine %[COLSP] 
```
... saves the current colorspace in a variable I have called "COLSP", then it separates into grayscale images, then it combines these into the original colorspace.

---
[c2] @bosonspace 2024-10-26T17:48:10Z:
Okay, thanks! It's helpful to understand that `-combine` always assumes sRGB when recombining. This explains part of the problem; i.e. the effect of using` -combine` after` -separate` performed on another color space than sRGB. This is not very clear in the options manual, but better explained here https://imagemagick.org/Usage/color_basics/#channels . Using `-combine` (which implies `+combine sRGB`) instead of `+combine Lab` also explains why no pixel values are transformed when applying `-colorspace sRGB`. 

Importantly, I also discovered now that the operation `-write image.jpg` silently transforms pixel values and sets color profile to sRGB in the saved image file (if current color space was set to something else than sRGB) while keeping the current color space in the pipe for the following operations! Which explains the result of my second command... Is this something relatively new?

With this in mind I still don't understand why rose2-Lab.jpg and rose2-RGB.jpg, from the second and fourth command respectively, does not provide the same looking image? When written to file, both should have pixel values converted to sRGB, from Lab and RGB respectively, saved with profile sRGB. 

My original issue actually concerns the use of `-profile` to convert from sRGB to Lab color space (and apply unsharp mask in the first channel) and then convert back to the sRGB color space (sixth command). Something has clearly been changed in IM7 so that the pixel values are not converted back into sRGB in the last step of the command!?

When converting from sRGB color space into Lab (transforming both pixel values and setting color profile) and saving this as sRGB I would expect something rather reddish like rose-profile1-Lab.jpg since luminance will be coded in the red channel. How can the cyan-bluish image be explained? If `-write image.jpg` operation converts and applies profile using IM native color space management it seems to clash with using external ICC profiles with `-profile`. If this is the case, how do I prevent `-write image.jpg` from doing color space conversion? 

PS: For clarity it should be `-write info:`.
---
[c3] @snibgo 2024-10-26T22:32:21Z:
> Importantly, I also discovered now that the operation -write image.jpg silently transforms pixel values and sets color profile to sRGB in the saved image file ...

Yes, although it isn't quite that simple. Data in a JPEG file is encoded as either YCbCr (for 3-channel images such as sRGB) or YCCK (for 4-channel images such as CMYK). But the JPEG library silently converts as required.

> ...  while keeping the current color space in the pipe for the following operations! Which explains the result of my second command... Is this something relatively new?

Yes, I think this is a fairly recent change. It used to be that "`-write x.jpg`" would change the image to be suitable for saving as a file. Other operations would operate on that changed image. By contrast, "`+write x.jpg`" would clone the image, change it to be suitable for saving, and then forget the clone. But I think "`-write x.jpg`" has changed to do the same as "`+write x.jpg`" .

> With this in mind I still don't understand why rose2-Lab.jpg and rose2-RGB.jpg, from the second and fourth command respectively, does not provide the same looking image? When written to file, both should have pixel values converted to sRGB, from Lab and RGB respectively, saved with profile sRGB.

Yes, I see what you mean. I think the problem is that JPEG doesn't record gamma, or the fact that the image is encoded as linear RGB instead of non-linear sRGB. So IM tells the JPEG library to save the linear RGB values, without converting to non-linear sRGB first. Any program reading that JPEG file will think the data is sRGB. That is my guess; I haven't looked that the code.

Regrading `-profile`: Lab profiles don't work as I think they should. Either that, or my brain is cracking up. I'm looking into this.

> PS: For clarity it should be -write info:.

Thanks for the correction. Yes, it needs the colon.

---
[c4] @snibgo 2024-10-27T10:38:39Z:
We might expect that a round-trip using profiles of sRGB -> Lab -> sRGB should take us back to where we started. But that doesn't happen.

The problem is how the a* and b* values are handled by IM and LCMS. After converting to Lab, these values can be negative. But when converting from Lab to sRGB, the values must not be negative. So a workaround is:
```
magick  rose: -profile sRGB.icc -profile lab.icc -channel 1,2 -evaluate Add 50% +channel -profile sRGB.icc out.tiff
```
By adding 50% of QuantumRange to the a* and b* channels, those values are transformed from the range [-50%,+50%] to [0,100%].

comments.author: snibgo
comments.body:
Your first command is:
```
magick rose: -set colorspace sRGB -colorspace LAB -separate -combine -write rose1-Lab.jpg -colorspace sRGB rose1-Lab-sRGB.jpg
```
> The above produces a rose1-Lab.jpg which is different to original rose image as is expected.

Yes. If you insert "`-write info:`" after "`-combine`", you will see that the image is at that point encoded as sRGB. But the pixel values are incorrect, of course.

(EDIT: Corrected "`-write info`" to "`-write info:`". It needs the colon.)

> However, quite unexpectedly rose1-Lab-sRGB.jpg looks the same as rose1-Lab.jpg.

This is expected. The image is encoded as sRGB, so "`-colorspace sRGB`" has no effect.

I think you misunderstand `-separate` and `-combine`. `-separate` replaces the current image, making one grayscale image per colour channel. The metadata describing the original colorspace is lost. `-combine` replaces the grayscale images with one colour image, and assumes the graycale images are sRGB channels. If they are not (as in your case) you should either use "`+combine Lab`", or "`-set colorspace Lab`" after the combine.

See https://imagemagick.org/script/command-line-options.php#combine

> Why is the result different between using options "-separate -combine"? Should not these two options after each other simply cancel out?

Those two together have no effect on pixel values. But they will change the colorspace metadata to sRGB.

Does that explain the problems?

The following sequence ...
```
-set option:COLSP %[colorspace] -separate +combine %[COLSP] 
```
... saves the current colorspace in a variable I have called "COLSP", then it separates into grayscale images, then it combines these into the original colorspace.

comments.author: bosonspace
comments.body:
Okay, thanks! It's helpful to understand that `-combine` always assumes sRGB when recombining. This explains part of the problem; i.e. the effect of using` -combine` after` -separate` performed on another color space than sRGB. This is not very clear in the options manual, but better explained here https://imagemagick.org/Usage/color_basics/#channels . Using `-combine` (which implies `+combine sRGB`) instead of `+combine Lab` also explains why no pixel values are transformed when applying `-colorspace sRGB`. 

Importantly, I also discovered now that the operation `-write image.jpg` silently transforms pixel values and sets color profile to sRGB in the saved image file (if current color space was set to something else than sRGB) while keeping the current color space in the pipe for the following operations! Which explains the result of my second command... Is this something relatively new?

With this in mind I still don't understand why rose2-Lab.jpg and rose2-RGB.jpg, from the second and fourth command respectively, does not provide the same looking image? When written to file, both should have pixel values converted to sRGB, from Lab and RGB respectively, saved with profile sRGB. 

My original issue actually concerns the use of `-profile` to convert from sRGB to Lab color space (and apply unsharp mask in the first channel) and then convert back to the sRGB color space (sixth command). Something has clearly been changed in IM7 so that the pixel values are not converted back into sRGB in the last step of the command!?

When converting from sRGB color space into Lab (transforming both pixel values and setting color profile) and saving this as sRGB I would expect something rather reddish like rose-profile1-Lab.jpg since luminance will be coded in the red channel. How can the cyan-bluish image be explained? If `-write image.jpg` operation converts and applies profile using IM native color space management it seems to clash with using external ICC profiles with `-profile`. If this is the case, how do I prevent `-write image.jpg` from doing color space conversion? 

PS: For clarity it should be `-write info:`.

comments.author: snibgo
comments.body:
> Importantly, I also discovered now that the operation -write image.jpg silently transforms pixel values and sets color profile to sRGB in the saved image file ...

Yes, although it isn't quite that simple. Data in a JPEG file is encoded as either YCbCr (for 3-channel images such as sRGB) or YCCK (for 4-channel images such as CMYK). But the JPEG library silently converts as required.

> ...  while keeping the current color space in the pipe for the following operations! Which explains the result of my second command... Is this something relatively new?

Yes, I think this is a fairly recent change. It used to be that "`-write x.jpg`" would change the image to be suitable for saving as a file. Other operations would operate on that changed image. By contrast, "`+write x.jpg`" would clone the image, change it to be suitable for saving, and then forget the clone. But I think "`-write x.jpg`" has changed to do the same as "`+write x.jpg`" .

> With this in mind I still don't understand why rose2-Lab.jpg and rose2-RGB.jpg, from the second and fourth command respectively, does not provide the same looking image? When written to file, both should have pixel values converted to sRGB, from Lab and RGB respectively, saved with profile sRGB.

Yes, I see what you mean. I think the problem is that JPEG doesn't record gamma, or the fact that the image is encoded as linear RGB instead of non-linear sRGB. So IM tells the JPEG library to save the linear RGB values, without converting to non-linear sRGB first. Any program reading that JPEG file will think the data is sRGB. That is my guess; I haven't looked that the code.

Regrading `-profile`: Lab profiles don't work as I think they should. Either that, or my brain is cracking up. I'm looking into this.

> PS: For clarity it should be -write info:.

Thanks for the correction. Yes, it needs the colon.

comments.author: snibgo
comments.body:
We might expect that a round-trip using profiles of sRGB -> Lab -> sRGB should take us back to where we started. But that doesn't happen.

The problem is how the a* and b* values are handled by IM and LCMS. After converting to Lab, these values can be negative. But when converting from Lab to sRGB, the values must not be negative. So a workaround is:
```
magick  rose: -profile sRGB.icc -profile lab.icc -channel 1,2 -evaluate Add 50% +channel -profile sRGB.icc out.tiff
```
By adding 50% of QuantumRange to the a* and b* channels, those values are transformed from the range [-50%,+50%] to [0,100%].

Tested with v6.9.12-72, v7.1.1-38 and earlier v7 versions, HDRI only. Integer iM may need different treatment.

Tested with Lab.icc posted in the OP, and Elle Stone's `Lab-D50-Identity-elle-V4.icc` from https://github.com/ellelstone/elles_icc_profiles/tree/master/profiles

title: Smartcrop is failing in latest ImageMagick
need_summary: Whether smartcrop-cli failing against newer ImageMagick on Windows is caused by the legacy convert command being removed, and the fix rests on the ImageMagick 7+ command mode change plus upgrading gm to 1.25.0.
security_topic: compatibility break with ImageMagick command invocation
question_text: Is there a way to print error, when magick is used in tools like smartcrop like a flag or something i can pass to debug the error.
answer_text:
The problem is, latest image magick no longer supports legacy "convert" command, and expects command to be "magick". To fix this, performed below actions,

1. Force gm(ghostMagick) to use "magick" comand, this is done by modifying to below code in, smarcrop-cli.js, index.js(smartcrop-gm), example.js(smartcrop-gm)
var gm = require('gm').subClass({ imageMagick: '7+' });
2. Upgraded gm to latest version 1.25.0 and also its corresponding dependencies.
After above 2 fixes, it is working fine.

title: Information in meta channel is lost when resizing a tiff
need_summary: Whether ImageMagick intentionally clears TIFF extra channels when reading Photoshop-created files, with the answer anchored on the documented `tiff:assume-alpha` define and the `TIFFTAG_EXTRASAMPLES`/`EXTRASAMPLE_UNSPECIFIED` explanation.
security_topic: TIFF extra-channel / alpha handling and data loss
question_text: I have several TIFF files with a meta channel (the meta channel is used as alpha channel). When I resize the files, the information in the meta channel is gone. It is becoming black.
answer_text: When we read a meta channel we will also write a meta channel. As mentioned before you can work around this with the `tiff:assume-alpha` define.
thread_text:
ISSUE #7616: Information in meta channel is lost when resizing a tiff
Author: gursch
Date: 2024-09-13T15:32:58Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

7.1.1-38 Q16 x64 b0ab922:20240901

### Operating system

Windows

### Operating system, version and so on

Windows 11 Pro 23H2

### Description

I have several TIFF files with a meta channel (the meta channel is used as alpha channel). When I resize the files, the information in the meta channel is gone. It is becoming black.

Channels in Photoshop before the conversion:
![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e829a961-24f6-4204-bc84-59dc636c9ea2)

After the conversion:
![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5430e7a-2352-414b-90df-1108525f5ca9)

See also: https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/discussions/7614

### Steps to Reproduce

magick test.tif -resize 500x500 out.tif

### Images

[test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16996134/test.zip)


--- COMMENTS ---
[c1] @snibgo 2024-09-13T18:16:55Z:
I confirm the problem.

`-resize` is not relevant. The problem can be shown by:
```
magick test.tif out.tif
```
... using IM v7.1.1-38 downloaded today, and then viewing test.tif and out.tif in Gimp. When opening the files, choose the default "Process extra channel as Non-premultiplied alpha". With test.tif, the area outside the banana is transparent. With out.tif, the entire image is transparent.

test.tif also has a clipping path around the apple. I don't know if that is relevant to the problem.

---
[c2] @snibgo 2024-09-16T04:19:06Z:
@gursch: How was test.tif created? Was it with Adobe Photoshop? 

A workaround for the misreading of the meta channel:
```
magick -define tiff:assume-alpha=true test.tif x.png
```
This will set the alpha channel to the correct values of the TIFF "extra" channel. The result is an opaque banana on a transparent background.

If you want, you can copy the alpha channel to a meta channel, and remove the alpha:
```
magick -define tiff:assume-alpha=true test.tif -channel-fx "alpha=>meta0" -alpha off x.tiff
```
(I save to a TIFF file, which can record meta channels. PNG can't.)

I have tested IM (v7.1.1-20 and v7.1.1-38) writing and reading TIFF RGB files, both 8-bit integer and 32-bit floating-point, with and without an alpha (opacity) channel, with one or two meta channels. IM writes and reads these files as expected. Gimp v2.10.34 (the current version) can read these files and shows correct results. (Gimp calls these channels "channel masks" or "selection masks".)

Gimp can't save meta channels ("channel masks") in TIFF files, so I can't test whether IM reads them correctly.

My conclusion: there is something in `test.tif` which causes IM to misread it, but only when IM tries to read it into a meta channel. I suspect the problem is in `coders/tiff.c`.

I don't have Photoshop. If you can provide further examples of images with meta channels, this will help us find the problem.

---
[c3] @dlemstra 2024-09-16T05:21:02Z:
The `TIFFTAG_EXTRASAMPLES` (one extra sample) are set to `EXTRASAMPLE_UNSPECIFIED` instead of `EXTRASAMPLE_ASSOCALPHA` or `EXTRASAMPLE_UNASSALPHA` and that means we don't treat the extra channel as an alpha channel. We added the `tiff:assume-alpha` option that you mentioned to allow the user to override the behavior.

The problem seems to be with the application that created those files.
---
[c4] @snibgo 2024-09-16T05:45:19Z:
> The TIFFTAG_EXTRASAMPLES (one extra sample) are set to EXTRASAMPLE_UNSPECIFIED instead of EXTRASAMPLE_ASSOCALPHA or EXTRASAMPLE_UNASSALPHA and that means we don't treat the extra channel as an alpha channel.

That is good behaviour from IM. But IM is then ignoring the values in that channel of the file. (Or IM is reading the values, but then setting them to zero.) That behaviour needs to be fixed.

Of course, if the file is bad in some way, then IM should reject it. It shouldn't create a meta channel (which is correct) but put the wrong values in that channel.

---
[c5] @gursch 2024-09-16T06:21:54Z:
Yes, the file was created with Photoshop.

We are currently using ImageMagick 7.1.0-28-Q16-x64 and I want to migrate to a more recent version. I used some old files (> 10 years) to test how ImageMagick deals with transparency and the outcome was, that many files are completely transparent (all values are set to zero). These images were working fine with the old version. Unfortunately I don't know if I can give these images away and therefore I build a new image to reproduce the issue using Photoshop. I think all of my test images were created using Photoshop.
I will try to gather more test images.
---
[c6] @gursch 2024-09-17T07:08:20Z:
I did some more tests with the different tiff options (tiff:alpha=associated, tiff:alpha=unassociated, tiff:alpha=unassociated) and the result is always that the alpha / meta channel gets empty.

I prepared two more test files:
- layers_rgb.tif (saved with tiff transparency OFF) 
- layers_rgb_with_tiff_transparency.tif (saved with tiff transparency ON)

[test2.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17024186/test2.zip)

Sorry, the screenshot is in German. When saving a TIFF file in Photoshop you have the option to store it with / without transparency. In the first file, the checkbox is not set.
![photoshop_tiff_save](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b968350-a96d-4889-b0f7-c9cfe9c14d63)

magick layers_rgb.tif out.tif -> creates a tiff file where the meta channel is getting cleared.
magick layers_rgb_with_tiff_transparency.tif out.tif -> creates a tiff file where the meta channel is applied as alpha channel and then cleared.

I think not setting the content of the meta channel to null would be a good solution. Many applications are using the meta channel as alpha channel and show the whole image as empty.

---
[c7] @dlemstra 2024-09-25T05:52:17Z:
When we read a meta channel we will also write a meta channel. As mentioned before you can work around this with the `tiff:assume-alpha` define.
---
