title: CVE-2024-41817 References Wrong ImageMagick Version
need_summary: Whether CVE-2024-41817 is a false positive for Windows binaries, anchored on the maintainer’s clarification that the advisory was corrected to 7.1.1-36 and affects only the Linux magick AppImage pre-7.1.1-36.
security_topic: applicability of CVE to Windows binaries versus Linux AppImage builds
question_text: Please advise if this is a false-positive.
answer_text: The vulnerability does not impact Windows binaries and should be considered a false positive in that context. It affects only Linux systems and specifically the `magick` AppImage. The issue arises only if the AppImage version is pre-ImageMagick 7.1.1-36. Additionally, it requires that an unauthorized individual gains access to your host system and stealthily creates a malicious configuration file in the AppImage folder. Finally, the vulnerability can be exploited only if the user executes a specific `magick` command-line.
thread_text:
ISSUE #7568: CVE-2024-41817 References Wrong ImageMagick Version
Author: zomayadev
Date: 2024-08-19T21:16:26Z
Labels: 
State: closed

[c0]
### ImageMagick version

7.1.1-36

### Operating system

Windows

### Operating system, version and so on

Server 2019

### Description

A false-positive finding is being reported for ImageMagick v7.1.1-36. It appears that there may be a missing dot between the 1's in the version number. Hence, vulnerablitity scanners are recommending to update this application to the latest version of 7.11-36. I checked ImageMagick's website, and the latest version of this application is v7.1.1-36. 

Please advise if this is a false-positive.

[CVE-2024-41817](https://cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2024-41817)
NVD Published Date:
07/29/2024
NVD Last Modified:
07/29/2024
Source:
GitHub, Inc. https://github.com/ImageMagick/ImageMagick/security/advisories/GHSA-8rxc-922v-phg8

### Steps to Reproduce

Accrording to Tenable:

_ImageMagick is a free and open-source software suite, used for editing and manipulating digital images. The `AppImage` version `ImageMagick` might use an empty path when setting `MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH` and `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` environment variables while executing, which might lead to arbitrary code execution by loading malicious configuration files or shared libraries in the current working directory while executing `ImageMagick`. The vulnerability is fixed in 7.11-36._

I don't recall a version 7.11-36 of ImageMagick.

As part of our commitment to quality, this fix will also be included in the upcoming [beta releases of ImageMagick](https://imagemagick.org/archive/beta/) by tomorrow. Your patience and feedback are greatly appreciated.

title: [BUG] no decode delegate for this image format `JPEG'
need_summary: Whether the ImageMagick JPEG module failure is caused by mixing Alpine edge packages and which dependency version must be upgraded, based on the maintainer’s note that libjpeg-turbo 3.0 adds jpeg_enable_lossless and that edge/main is needed.
security_topic: dependency mismatch causing JPEG delegate loading failure
question_text:
With imagemagick `v7.1.1.35` everything works as it should.

but with `v7.1.1.36` i get this error when trying to do for example, the command below:

Error: 
`error/module.c/OpenModule/1293.
no decode delegate for this image format 'JPEG'`
answer_text: And just verified that `3.0.3-r0` of `libjpeg-turbo-dev`  is only available in the main repos, so you will need to add `http://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/edge/main` too.

7.1.1.36

Linux

# Add the Edge Community repository and update

This is one of the reasons why mixing the edge repo with a versioned repo is never recommended for alpine.

If you absolutely have to do it, the best way that I have found is to follow these steps in the upstream alpine:edge container:
* List all installed packages by default.
* Add all required packages that you want to test on edge.
* List the packages again.

title: Identify Error
need_summary: Whether the Identify/fx command failure was the known ImageMagick bug from issue #7491, and the concrete workaround was to use +ping or -colorspace sRGB because the current beta source code already contains the patch.
security_topic: image metadata/pixel-access failure causing fx expression to error
question_text:
I just updated my installation.
I have used this code to get min width or height of image. It is now failing. Error below.


_magick identify -format "%[fx:min(w,h)]" test.jpg_

identify: GetHslInt failure 0 0,0 @ error/fx.c/ExecuteRPN/3159.
identify: ExecuteRPN failed   @ error/fx.c/FxEvaluateChannelExpression/4022.


**update:** I found a workaround or the requirement has changed. The following code works as expected.

_magick identify -colorspace sRGB -format "%[fx:min(w,h)]" test.jpg_
answer_text:
`+ping` is the simplest workaround, as it ensures pixels are read, with no other effects. `-colorspace sRGB` will also ensure pixels are read, but will also change the colorspace to sRGB (with three colour channels) if it isn't already.

The current (Beta) source code should work fine, with no workarounds needed.

title: Unrecoverable error: ioerror in setdistillerparams
need_summary: Whether upgrading Ghostscript is necessary because the installed 9.54.0 library contains a remote code execution vulnerability, and the answer rests on the maintainer’s comment in [c8].
security_topic: Ghostscript library linkage and upgrade guidance for a PDF conversion error
question_text:
Did a yum update recently and immediately started getting errors - something about ImageMagick and Ghostscript. Ghostscript wasn't installed ... strange. We downloaded and compiled Ghostscript and everything worked. Then we realized that yum had a ghostscript install so we installed that. ImageMagick broke. We uninstalled everything and reinstalled everything - still isn't working... yes we tried to re-complile ghostscript again - nothing will fix this so far.

Background: We use ImageMagick to convert PDFs to JPGs (preview a PDF image on a website). Has worked for years and suddenly stopped. We upgraded and downgraded ghostscript and ImageMagick serveral times and can NOT fix this problem.
answer_text:
ImageMagick is linked with Ghostscript and that is why you are seeing: `[ghostscript library 95.40]`. I would first recommend you to upgrade Ghostscript. The version you are using contains a remote code execution vulnerability. This might also fix that error.

If that doesn't resolve the issue you could consider recompiling ImageMagick with `--with-gslib` to make sure you are always using the command line version of Ghostscript instead of the library calls.
